title: Watford set to appoint former Romania boss Iordanescu
description: Watford are set to appoint former Romania coach Edward Iordanescu as their new head coach, reports BBC Three Counties Radio.
article_context:
Edward Iordanescu's most recent job was with Legia Warsaw, who he left in October 2025
Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager.
BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge.
The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT).
Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16.
Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025.
It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland.
Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.
Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.
The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.
The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

title: Morocco and Senegal await Afcon final verdict after court case
description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport is set to rule on the decision to strip Senegal of the Afcon 2025 title.
article_context:
Sadio Mane was named best player at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations
Everyone knows a football match should take 90 minutes, but the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations has been playing out for 10 months.
Now, finally, Morocco or Senegal will be crowned winners. However, that moment of glory will come in a courtroom, not on the pitch.
On Tuesday afternoon sport's highest legal authority, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), will render its judgement on Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip them of the title they thought they won in January against the hosts in Rabat.
The case was heard in early October, and the wait is almost over.
With 66,000 fans creating an electric atmosphere in the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Morocco were chasing their first Afcon title since 1976.
But the final descended into chaos deep into second-half stoppage time.
With the match goalless, Senegal thought Ismaila Sarr had scored a dramatic winner, only to discover that referee Jean Jacques Ndala had blown for a Morocco free-kick.
The controversy deepened in the 98th minute when, after a video assistant referee (VAR) review, Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty.
Tempers boiled over on the touchline and in the stands. Senegal coach Pape Thiaw led some of his players and staff down the tunnel, while supporters clashed with security as order briefly collapsed.
Play eventually resumed and, in the 124th minute, Morocco missed a golden chance to end their 50-year wait for continental glory when Brahim Diaz failed to convert a penalty, chipping it 'Panenka' style into the arms of goalkeeper Edouard Mendy.
Pape Gueye's extra-time strike then secured a 1-0 win for Senegal, who lifted the trophy for a second time.
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FMRF) quickly lodged a complaint with the Confederation of African Football (Caf), arguing that Senegal had breached competition regulations.
Article 82, contained within a chapter titled 'Withdrawals', states: "If, for any reason whatsoever, a team... refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee", they shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated from the current competition".
In March a Caf appeals board agreed, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory.
While there is precedent for Caf overturning results during Afcon and World Cup qualifying, some people, including one former senior Caf official, argued that only the referee has the authority to abandon a match if a walk-off occurs.
The FMRF said it was seeking the proper application of tournament regulations, but Senegal's federation (FSF) described the ruling as "unfair, unprecedented and unacceptable" and appealed to Cas.
Some Senegal supporters were initially convicted of hooliganism offences after clashes during the final but eventually returned home after receiving a royal pardon
Founded in 1984 and based in the Swiss city of Lausanne, Cas was set up as an independent legal body designed to settle disputes as global sport became more lucrative and, as a result, more litigious.
For governing bodies which recognise Cas' authority, it is deemed to be the supreme arbiter, meaning its ruling is final unless, in rare cases, Switzerland's highest court decides to set it aside based on a limited number of technicalities.
More than 900 cases are filed every year, from more than 50 different sports, covering issues such as employment contracts and transfers, doping, corruption, TV rights and, in this case, the organisation of sporting events.
The FSF's appeal was heard in private on 8 October by a panel of three arbitrators chosen by Cas for their expertise in sports law.
The panel was led by Frenchman Gerald Simon, founder of the Sports Law Laboratory at the University of Burgundy and a Cas member for 23 years.
Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of ​law at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas completed the trio.
If the panel had failed to come to a consensus on the case, Cas president Simon will have made the final decision.
Although Caf's appeals board is independent, a reversal of its judgement would deliver another blow to the reputation of African football's governing body, which has been heavily criticised for the retrospective decision to hand Morocco the title.
Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in March that it will "adhere to" and "respect" whatever Cas decides, so, if things go in Senegal's favour, it could mean someone having to tinker with the Afcon rulebook.
The Senegal walk-off has, however, already brought about a change in football's rules.
"The referee may sanction with a red card any player who leaves the field of play in protest at ⁠a ​referee's decision," said Ifab, the game's lawmaking body, in April.
"This new rule will also apply ​to any team official who incites players to leave the field of play. A team that causes a match ​to be abandoned will, in principle, forfeit the match."
Thiaw lost his job following Senegal's last-32 World Cup exit this summer, while Walid Regragui, the man in the Morocco dugout in January, was dismissed in March.
Whatever the outcome of the case, animosity is likely to linger between the two federations.
The FMRF's senior hierarchy was furious with Senegal's behaviour, believing the pictures beamed around the world irrevocably tarnished the image of the first Afcon hosted by the kingdom since 1988 - a tournament into which a huge amount of time and money had been invested.
The FSF and the Senegalese government have leaned into a feeling prevalent across the continent that Morocco holds too much influence within African football.
Other incidents also irked Senegal, such as laser pens being directed into players' eyes and ball boys moving goalkeeper Mendy's towel, something which led to the barely believable sight of reserve keeper Yehvann Diouf being tackled to the ground by three ball boys when he tried to intervene.
With the next Afcon scheduled to take place in June and July next year, the chances of a high-profile rematch between Africa's best two teams is a tantalising thought.
While the chaos of this year's final may have given birth to a new rivalry for fans to revel in, there is unanimous agreement that such encounters should be settled on the pitch and not in a courtroom.

title: Four Midlands teams in the Championship top five - can it last?
description: With more than a third of the season gone, Stoke City, Birmingham City, Wolves and West Brom are all in the Championship promotion race. Who can keep it up?
article_context:
Mark Robins (Stoke City), Cesar Peixoto (Wolves), Chris Davies (Birmingham City) and James Morrison (West Bromwich Albion) all have cause to feel content
It is beginning to look a lot like Christmas for followers of Midlands football.
Granted, it is actually only November, but with more than a third of the 2026-27 Championship season gone, already the table is taking on an increasingly familiar weekly look in terms of the primary promotion contenders.
There has been many a year when there have been early-season stirrings in the Midlands, only for the momentum to fade.
But Coventry City proved it can be done after 25 years away from the Premier League. And now Stoke City, Wolves, Birmingham City and West Bromwich Albion are all in contention to join both the Sky Blues and Aston Villa in the top flight.
Stoke in second, Wolves third, Blues fourth and Albion fifth makes for both a heartening, yet surprising sight, with only Middlesbrough in front of them.
It is only six months since Wolves were relegated and, for all the summer discontent at Molineux and doubts among disillusioned fans about their worthiness as serious candidates, the fact is they are very much in the mix.
But, while most people at Molineux can now at least contemplate a quick return, for their local rivals the parachute payments have long since expired.
Blues have been away the longest, their 15-year absence from the top flight having even included a one-season return to the third tier and back.
But, given their extensive American backing, the club have ambitions to be serious contenders - and the only surprise was that it took so long to find their feet.
For Stoke and Albion to be up there was not necessarily forecast, but it has made for all the more happy motoring for the BBC correspondents who cover the quartet of clubs on a regular basis.
BBC Sport asked reporters from BBC Stoke & Staffordshire and BBC West Midlands Sport for their analysis of the season so far and what lies in store for each club...
Next five fixtures: Millwall (H), West Ham (A), QPR (H), Lincoln (A), West Brom (H)
Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: 16th, 15th, 14th, 14th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 17th
American midfielder Jack McGlynn (centre, smiling) is Stoke's top scorer, having hit Championship goals in 10 starts for Stoke, shading the three from defender Ben Wilmot (right)
Mark Robins has spoken a lot about evolution and incremental gains in his time as Stoke City manager, but it's hard to escape the feeling that there's been a full-blown revolution over the past three months.
Stoke began the season with three defeats, a manager under pressure and the impending loss of their most productive player in Sorba Thomas - but a change in formation, an excellent summer transfer window and an unbelievable run of form has quietened all dissenting voices.
Thirty two out of a possible 39 points from 13 games since the window closed is a brilliant record - but Stoke are maybe still short of truly turning the hopefully optimistic among their fans into true believers.
Most of that is a hangover from last season's promising start eventually falling apart, but there are substantial differences.
The squad has more quality and depth, a more ambitious way of playing and the less quantifiable qualities of tenacity and resilience and a mental strength that, coupled with defensive solidity, has allowed them to find multiple ways to win close games.
Luke Graham, Ethan Galbraith, Jack McGlynn and Ben Johnson have been their most eye-catching summer acquisitions but several who struggled last season, Eric Bocat first among them, have found success too.
The next step is to create more chances and score more goals, whilst maintaining anything close to their current return of points per game.
Even the most hardened pessimists will then maybe see a play-off place as a realistic aim for 2027.
Next five fixtures: Derby (H), Lincoln (A), Southampton (H), QPR (A), Millwall (H)
Championship finishes since last in the Premier League: Relegated (2026)
In-form Adam Armstrong's strike at Wrexham was part of a run of four goals in five games
Only a point behind, and with the feeling they have not played to their full ability very often yet - not very often for 90 consecutive minutes, certainly - Wolves are not badly placed.
Their supporters can be hard taskmasters at the moment, and can hardly be blamed for that in view of the mess of recent seasons and the big promises made of going full-tilt to get straight back up.
For all the understandable misgivings, though, there is a clear path towards achieving it.
Reaching the end of that path may require some judicious spending in January to tidy up a squad that still looks imbalanced, with a surfeit of players in some areas and a shortage in others.
Personal surges in form, from Fer Lopez early in the season to Adam Armstrong more recently, have covered up the gaps and reminded everyone that this squad is not short of class at this level.
Cesar Peixoto, new to England, has handled a delicate situation in a tumultuous league with quiet confidence.
He will have to complete the job in May before he can claim credit more widely, but appears to realise the power he can harness if, like a certain Portuguese predecessor, he can unify all the forces around the club to point in the same direction.
Wolves' Mane of the moment has to now kick on
Next five fixtures: Burnley (A), Bolton (H), Charlton (A), Watford (H), Portsmouth (A)
Finishes since last in the Premier League: Fourth (lost to Blackpool in play-offs), 12th, 21st, 10th, 10th, 19th, 19th, 17th, 20th, 18th, 20th, 17th, 22nd, League One champions, 10th
Blues top scorer August Priske has netted six goals in 12 starts this season
For all of the outside noise about the future of Chris Davies, the Birmingham City board have steadfastly backed their man. Now that decision is paying dividends.
Thanks to that rarely tried footballing trait of continuity, they spent the international break sitting at the top of a very congested Championship table.
But Saturday's 1-0 loss against 10-man Stoke was a reminder of just how tight the division is.
The reboot of the squad started in earnest in January, when the future for Davies was at its wobbliest.

title: Dead hippo to be honoured on football club tifo
description: Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.
article_context:
Fiona first rose to fame when she was born premature at Cincinnati Zoo in 2017
Major League Soccer side FC Cincinnati will honour Fiona, a hippo that recently died at the city's zoo, with a tifo display at their match with Nashville SC on Saturday.
Fiona, a social media star since her premature birth at the zoo in 2017, died on Thursday after swallowing a woollen hat that had slipped into her enclosure.
The Ohio side will now raise a banner depicting the nine-year-old semi-aquatic mammal in their post-season MLS Cup encounter with Nashville, who won the Supporters' Shield for being the highest-placed team in the league campaign.
Cincinnati said Fiona was a "beloved hippo who became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world".
The tifo will be produced by fan group The Forge Cincy, who painted the display on Sunday in a garage next to Cincinnati's TQL Stadium.
The club will also make a donation in Fiona's memory for every fan in attendance to the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden.
Fan group The Forge Cincy had previously spent two weeks creating a tifo for their "Hell is Real" October derby match against Ohio rivals Columbus
Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says
Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
Cincinnati's Nick Hagglund, who hails from the city and is in his eighth season with the team, previously paid tribute to Fiona after scoring in his side's 3-1 victory over Orlando on the day of her death.
The defender yelled "that's for Fiona", mimicking the ears on top of her head, in a celebration video , external on the club's Instagram.
Later, on his Instagram account , external , Hagglund posted, "This one was for her @fionahippo @cincinnatizoo.
"Cincinnati needed a win on the day after the passing of our beloved hippo, a symbol of hope and resilience for our city, and the lads answered the call."
Cincinnati's tifo is one of a number of tributes paid to the hippo, with Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins wearing a Fiona sweater , external prior to his American football franchise's defeat by the Washington Commanders on Monday.
Meanwhile handlers of the blue hippo balloon at New York's annual Macy's Thanksgiving Parade will wear a purple patch in her honour.
At birth, Fiona weighed 13kg (29lb), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species, and she previously inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.
From premature baby to social media star - famed Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies
Fiona swallowed the woollen hat around 10 days prior to her death, with the item getting into her enclosure by accident after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.
"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.
Hippos normally live up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.
Nashville finished top of the MLS Eastern Conference, 31 points ahead of ninth-placed Cincinnati.
However, having beaten Orlando in a one-off wildcard round, Cincinnati defeated Nashville 1-0 in the opening match of their best-of-three round one series.
Should Cincinnati win on Saturday they will progress to a one-off conference semi-final with either Chicago Fire or Charlotte FC, with a conference final prior to the season-ending MLS Cup final.

title: Barnet forward Noel-Williams charged with rape
description: Isiah Noel-Williams, from St Albans, is remanded in custody charged with three rape offences.
article_context:
Isiah Noel-Williams has been remanded in custody
League Two footballer Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with rape.
Noel-Williams, who plays for League Two side Barnet, has been charged with three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault by penetration, Hertfordshire Police said.
The 23-year-old, of High Oaks, St Albans, was remanded in custody following a hearing at Hatfield Magistrates' Court on Saturday.
In a statement, the club said it was "co-operating fully with authorities" and would determine further action "in due course".
Noel-Williams has also been charged with one count of engaging in sexual communication with a child, and one count of supplying a controlled (Class B) drug, police added.
In a statement, the London club said: "Barnet FC can confirm that first-team player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged and remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary.
"The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.
"As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment."
Noel-Williams, who previously played for Hemel Hempstead Town, Kettering Town, Matlock Town, Harrow Borough and Cheshunt, joined Barnet in June.

title: Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years
description: When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wendesday they are likely to come up against English midfelder Freddie Potts.
article_context:
Freddie Potts has started all of Club Brugge's Champions League games
When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.
The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.
And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.
After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.
"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.
"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."
Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.
Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.
He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.
"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.
"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.
"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.
"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."
Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.
"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.
"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."
Freddie Potts on leaving West Ham, life in Belgium and beating Inter Milan
Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.
And he revealed he has a lifelong history with the city.
"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.
"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.
"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."
Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.
The Reds are eighth and Club Brugge are ninth in the table.
"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.
"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

title: Crystal Palace docked three WSL points for extra substitution against Everton

title: Two goals in 15 games - what's going on with Gyokeres?
description: Arsenal have made an impressive start to the campaign but it has been a frustrating one for striker Viktor Gyokeres.
article_context:
Viktor Gyokeres has scored twice in all competitions this season
A Premier League trophy and 21 goals in his debut season - on paper things have worked out perfectly for Viktor Gyokeres since his £64m transfer to Arsenal.
But, even with those achievements, it has been a tough start to the current campaign for the 28-year-old striker.
The Swede has started just one Premier League game this season and is yet to score in his eight league appearances.
He has started three games in the Champions League, two in the Carabao Cup, and has scored just twice in 15 games in all competitions. Not the numbers he would have hoped for after last season's glory.
It is not just this season that has seen Gyokeres suitability questioned for Arsenal though.
Even though he scored more than 20 goals in his first season in all competitions as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for a title, his all-round game had its critics.
It has been near enough a straight battle for the number nine role between Kai Havertz and Gyokeres since the Swedish international signed.
And Gyokeres was thrust into leading the line for Arsenal quicker and more frequently than planned after injury kept Havertz out for long periods last season.
Although the Swede may be the more natural finisher, Havertz's all-round play is considered superior with the German also one of Arteta's most trusted players for big games.
Gyokeres, a "win-now signing", was bought for his ability to find the net but also for how he could open up spaces for his team-mates, something they have praised him for.
But playing with his back to goal and linking up play is not natural to Gyokeres and his failure to hold up the ball or win duels with centre-backs has led to fan frustration.
Arteta has spoken about how the striker has been working on improving his hold-up play and connections, and there were hints of it in the Champions League win over Slavia Prague where Gyokeres assisted the opener and scored the winner in arguably his best game of the season.
Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'
A big reason that Gyokeres is not starting games is that Havertz is fit.
Last season, Havertz suffered with knee and hamstring issues which meant Gyokeres was the only option Arteta had.
Had Havertz been fit, he would have played a lot more and the fact that he started the Champions League final and the key match away at Manchester City in last season's title race back this up.
This season Gyokeres has just six starts and Arteta says that his gametime and situation is similar to other members in the squad.
"We have rotated the team a lot and used the competitions as well to give minutes to players and exposure because they are all starters in my opinion," Arteta said.
"Viktor's case is one of many that they have been in the same situation where they play more in the Premier League or more in the Champions League which is not bad, eh?"
Arteta is open with his players about their standing in the squad and said that Gyokeres has not approached him directly about a lack of minutes.
"We have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing and to gather information about the way we are feeling and so far it has been very positive with Viktor and the rest of the team," he said.
The signing of Gyokeres is an interesting one in its own right.
The Arsenal recruitment team had done a lot of due diligence on signing, now Manchester United forward, Benjamin Sesko.
It is understood work on that deal had been done but a change of direction to sign Gyokeres happened after Andrea Berta became Arsenal sporting director.
Some around Arsenal have always thought that Gyokeres is not the usual forward that the Gunners would go for and his predicament of a lack of game time was always likely to happen, even if he did play a big part in them ending their trophy drought.
Gyokeres ended last season with 14 league goals but those strikes actually only won Arsenal two points on their way to winning the league.
That is because, although his penalty in the 1-0 win at Everton was the only goal of the game, Arsenal would have come away with a draw, so that strike factually only accounted for two points and not three.
But Gyokeres did put the Gunners ahead five times last season in the league which shows that, among the frustrating performances, he had plenty of impact.
Max Dowman stole the show with his goal in the 2-0 home win over Everton , when he became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, but it was Gyokeres' goal in the 89th-minute which put Arsenal ahead and although it did not lead to a point score on its own, it set them on the way.
Gyokeres also scored in the 4-1 north London derby win, putting Arsenal ahead when Kolo Muani had equalised after Eberechi Eze's opener.
It is unlikely that Gyokeres will be sold in January as he continues to get games in the Champions League and is a senior player who can score goals in big moments.
But if his lack of minutes in the league continue, Gyokeres, who is a driven and ambitious individual, will not want to be the player who is left out of the starting XI in the long term.
Additional reporting Chris Collinson, BBC Sport Football data analyst and Sami Mokbel senior football correspondent.

title: Can returning Beattie and Haughey make an impact?
description: BBC Sport NI looks at Michael McArdle's decision to recall striker Kerry Beattie and the uncapped Ella Haughey to his squad for a friendly double-header against Greece.
article_context:
Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021
Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.
Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.
Beattie won her last cap a year ago while Haughey will hope to make a senior debut in one of the two games against Greece at Inver Park after she was an unused substitute in friendlies against England and Scotland in her sole call up in 2021.
The inclusion of both players, who have been in good form at their clubs, shows McArdle is willing to keep the door open for a return to the international squad if players are performing at club level.
Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies
Portsmouth striker Beattie has been in and out of squads since her debut in 2021.
The 24-year-old has four goals in 13 caps, the last of which she won against Iceland in the Nations League play-off a year ago.
A prolific forward during two spells at Glentoran, she has struggled for consistency in moves across to Scotland with the likes of Glasgow City, Hearts and Aberdeen.
She left the Dons in the summer and consulted with McArdle when deciding upon her next move, before joining WSL 2 side Portsmouth.
Beattie has eight goals in all competitions for a Pompey side languishing at the bottom of the table and McArdle is pleased she has settled in well.
"Kerry had spells at Hearts and Aberdeen and for whatever reason it didn't quite work out at both, she had good spells but not a consistent run to express herself," McArdle said.
"The move to Portsmouth, I was delighted she reached out to me for some advice, it's an alignment for her and it's been a great move on and off the pitch. It's allowed her to enjoy herself but also play 90 minutes and be that focal point striker.
"She will have been disappointed not to make the squad for the [World Cup] play-off [against Portugal] with her form but she worked hard and she's back in, I'm delighted for her."
Beattie faces stiff competition for the starting striker role from the likes of returning captain Simone Magill and Kess Elmore, who impressed in the last camp and scored against Portugal, but she should receive some minutes across the two games and will be keen to grasp her chance to make an impact.
Left-back Haughey was called up to the senior squad as a 16-year-old under Kenny Shiels, but did not feature
West Brom defender Haughey's last involvement with NI came when she represented the under-19s in 2023.
A Lisburn Rangers player when Kenny Shiels included her in the senior squad as a 16-year-old, Haughey then moved to Nottingham Forest before settling at the Baggies, who play in the National League.
The left-back, 22, has been a regular this season for the club in the third tier and combines playing with her university studies.
Left-back has been a problem position for NI which McArdle has been trying to address as demonstrated by him bringing in Lucy-Jayne Grant in the last camp and Haughey for this window to allow Rebecca Holloway to play as a central defender.
Haughey will be competing with Grant to fill that full-back role on the left side and McArdle believes she is more than capable of doing so having tried to bring her back into the squad earlier in his reign.
"Ella's been at West Brom for a few years now. She has real potential, strong, athletic potential. We tried to call her up sooner but there were some challenges," he explained.
"She's probably been one of their top performers and one of the top performers in the league. Delighted she's earned this opportunity and hopefully she can make her debut and achieve her first cap."
McArdle has made a concerted to continue to widen the player pool available to him as he aims to build depth ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, but if Beattie and Haughey catch the eye it will show that giving chances to those previously involved under different managers could be another possibility.

title: Why has De Bruyne struggled at Napoli as he returns to Man City?
description: Kevin de Bruyne's move to Napoli last summer was supposed to mark a continuation of his glittering decade at Manchester City as he approaches the twilight years of his career.
article_context:
Kevin de Bruyne won 16 trophies in 10 years at Manchester City
Kevin de Bruyne's move to Napoli in 2025 was supposed to mark a continuation of his glittering decade at Manchester City as he approaches the twilight years of his career.
Instead, the midfielder, who is widely regarded as one of the standout players of his generation, has seen his time in Naples threaten to turn sour amid an early injury, friction with his team-mates and rumours of a January exit.
Napoli were Serie A champions in 2024-25 - the year before De Bruyne's arrival - but are currently languishing in eighth, while they sit 27th in the Champions League after a heavy 4-1 defeat at Porto earlier this month.
Belgium international De Bruyne lifted 16 trophies in his 10 years at City and is guaranteed a generous ovation when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday but the highs of his time in England are in contrast to the struggles he is seemingly enduring in Italy.
"Not a lot I can say for the moment," said De Bruyne when asked about his future. "I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.
"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening."
De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'
Statue, Pep's tears & a missed sitter - De Bruyne's emotional farewell
City decided not to renew De Bruyne's contract during the 2024-25 season and the player had the choice of heading to the US with Chicago Fire or staying in one of the top-five leagues in Europe.
The 35-year-old felt he could still cut it at the highest level but his first season at Napoli was heavily disrupted by a hamstring injury which kept him out for more than four months, restricting him to 21 appearances.
Napoli finished runners up to Inter Milan to lose their Serie A title and De Bruyne reportedly said , external he was "happy" manager Antonio Conte had departed in the summer as promises were not kept regarding the style of play.
But despite making his name as a technically gifted number 10, De Bruyne's role has been remodelled into a deeper holding one under Massimiliano Allegri in an ageing squad that has struggled this season.
In Porto, the fractures were clear to see, with De Bruyne having a heated on-field confrontation , external with striker Lorenzo Lucca and his team-mates were forced to step in to diffuse the situation.
The passionate side of De Bruyne's game was shown in Manchester too.
The midfielder shouted "shut up" at manager Pep Guardiola during a Champions League game against Real Madrid in 2023, and said "let me talk" when David Silva and Fernandinho were ushering him off the pitch at half-time shortly after he was booked against Napoli in 2017.
"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli," Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino tells BBC Sport. "The point is that the whole team is having difficulties.
"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.
"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show."
De Bruyne has played 16 times for Napoli this season - contributing four goals and two assists - but his long-term future at the club remains unclear.
In September, De Bruyne's wife reportedly , external told a Belgian publication about their desire to move back home, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as the player leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.
Asked if the quotes had been misinterpreted, De Bruyne said: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.
"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.
"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family."
It has led to interest from the Netherlands with PSV Eindhoven making a £1.67m offer to sign him in January, but the two clubs are apart in their valuations as Napoli want up to £6.7m, according to Credendino.
"Napoli fans were not happy [with the interview]," he says. "There are many fans that say, 'OK, you can leave if you want, we are not putting chains on anybody'."
Napoli boss Allegri left the door open for a January exit by saying in his pre-match news conference the pair had "not spoken" about his future and it is "down to the players and who wants to leave" when the transfer window opens.
City manager Enzo Maresca was assistant to Pep Guardiola during the 2022-23 campaign in which De Bruyne helped the club to a Treble of trophies and the Italian has fond memories of the "fantastic season" they spent together.
"No doubt, [he is] one of the best," Maresca said of De Bruyne in his pre-match news conference. "Not only personally but also for the history of this club. In the last 10 years all the trophies the club achieved Kevin was here.
"He was an important player, a top guy, polite and for me it was a pleasure to work with him."
This is not the first time De Bruyne will be facing his former club with a reunion with City in the Champions League last season.
That trip turned out to be a bitterly unhappy experience, with De Bruyne substituted after 26 minutes following Giovanni di Lorenzo's red card in the 2-0 defeat.
The midfielder will be hoping for a better result on Tuesday as he aims to park his struggles for one evening.
City and Belgium winger Jeremy Doku said: "Kevin is someone that likes football. Even at this age he loves it.
"I don't have any doubts about his quality and I am sure everything will be fine in Napoli."

title: Defender Heaven open to leaving Man Utd
description: Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.
article_context:
Heaven has made 32 appearances for Manchester United
Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.
The 20-year-old centre-back is concerned about what United's current situation means for his development, after new manager Mauricio Pochettino left him as an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool .
Now on his third manager in 21 months since joining from Arsenal in February 2025, Heaven accepts Pochettino may prefer more experienced options as United attempt to avoid a shock relegation.
The club have also been heavily linked with signing a centre-back in the coming January window, with targets said to include Fulham 's Calvin Bassey.
However, the Cottagers regard Bassey as an important player and would not encourage any interest.
Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal .
The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.
At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.
Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.
He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.

title: Man United win appeal over Yoro red card against Liverpool
description: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
article_context:
Manchester United have won their appeal over Leny Yoro 's red card against Liverpool .
The Frenchman was dismissed after eight minutes at Anfield after a challenge on Alexander Isak . On-field referee Sam Barrott decided Yoro had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity, a view backed up by VAR John Brooks.
United, who lost 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach, launched an appeal on Monday, insisting that Isak's heavy touch meant he would not have had the chance to score.
The Football Association announced on Tuesday that the claim of wrongful dismissal has been upheld and Yoro's one-match ban has been lifted.
A statement issued by the FA read: "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday Nov. 22."
Bruno Fernandes told the BBC that it was "never a red card," adding: "I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.
"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."
Pochettino said: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control."
Kobbie Mainoo added: "The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is."
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola defended the referee's decision, saying: "[Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."
It's the second major refereeing error in a game involving United this season. In September, referee's body Pro Ref apologised after Erling Haaland 's goal at Old Trafford was mistakenly allowed to stand.
City, who were reduced to 10 men in the first half after Phil Foden 's red card, won the game 1-0.
headline: Manchester United anula suspensión de Leny Yoro
caption: La sanción de un partido impuesta a Leny Yoro tras su expulsión contra Liverpool ha sido revocada después de que la FA aceptara la apelación del club. El defensor francés, expulsado en los ocho minutos iniciales por negar una clara oportunidad de gol, recupera su disponibilidad para el próximo encuentro de la Premier League.

title: Women's World Cup returning to U.S. shows how the game has grown since 1999
description: Women's soccer was forever changed when the U.S. hosted the 1999 World Cup. With it returning in 2031, ESPN charts the game's explosive growth.
article_context:
The Women's World Cup is coming back to the United States, with FIFA making the announcement Monday that the U.S., along with Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico will be co-hosting the 2031 edition of the tournament .
The 2031 World Cup will mark the first time that 48 teams will compete for the trophy, signifying the immense growth that women's soccer has enjoyed in recent years.
"This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world," said U.S. Soccer president Cindy Parlow Cone. "Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams."
As such, it will have been 32 years since the U.S. first hosted the competition, when Brandi Chastain's iconic celebration capped off an epic run to the title by the U.S. women's national team . (The U.S. hosted the 2003 edition as well due to the SARS pandemic). Suffice it to say, the paths the women's game has trodden since make "The Odyssey" look like a Sunday cruise.
The U.S. witnessed two domestic leagues go under. Each failure seemed like a death knell for the sport, leaving fans to wonder whether there would ever be a viable club competition for the country's best players. Even as the third attempt, the NWSL , struggled to survive, it was deeply wounded by a sex abuse scandal . That outrage left scars that for some won't ever fully heal.
Yet the women's game has been nothing if not resilient. At club level, new investment poured into the NWSL, and with it, a level of stability and media attention that seemed unfathomable a decade ago. The league reported that total regular-season attendance rose to 2.5 million. According to Forbes, team valuations now average $200 million .
The developments abroad have been even more encouraging. For the first two decades after that fateful 1999 World Cup, the U.S. was the dominant power. The Americans won four World Cups in total and claimed another four Olympic gold medals following their victory in the inaugural competition in 1996.
As euphoric as those wins were for U.S. fans, it didn't necessarily speak to a healthy competition on a worldwide basis. But eventually, investment in other countries began to increase. Clubs in Spain, England and Mexico dedicated more resources to the women's game, and as a consequence rose up to challenge the sport's traditional powers, including the likes of the U.S., Japan , France and others.
That increase in investment and competition has seen some tangible results. Earlier this year, Club América claimed the Concacaf W Champions Cup, beating Gotham FC and the Washington Spirit along the way. At international level, Spain has assumed the mantle of the best women's national team in the world, claiming its first World Cup in 2023.
The oft-discussed gap between the USWNT and the rest of the world has vanished. Yes, the U.S. claimed Olympic gold again in 2024, but just a year before exited the World Cup in the round of 16. Claiming the top spot on the podium can no longer be expected like it was in the past.
That has resulted in plenty of introspection in the United States. The college game in the U.S. was once viewed as the gold standard for developing players. Not so now with players elsewhere entering professional environments at younger and younger ages.
Ali Krieger, Cristina Alexander and Jeff Kassouf debate the biggest storylines and break down the best highlights from women's soccer in the Americas. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only)
This is a healthy development for women's soccer. Steel sharpens steel, as the saying goes, and forcing clubs, leagues and other stakeholders to innovate to stay competitive is vital to the sport's overall growth.
That prospect is what makes the next five years so exciting. There are challenges to be sure. The fight for a bigger slice of resources -- from wages to sponsorship to infrastructure -- is never ending, but the trend in terms of gaining a bigger piece of those investments is decidedly upward.
Those benefits look set to extend to the U.S.'s co-hosts. Much like the men's World Cup in 2026, the U.S. figures to host the vast majority of matches, but at the very least, there will more eyeballs and interest in the countries that are co-hosting.
The five-year window before the tournament kicks off provides a lengthy on-ramp in terms of securing sponsorship and generating interest. On the field, will countries like Colombia , Morocco and Portugal continue to develop and threaten to further upset the status quo?
Women's soccer has navigated a challenging path to get to its current, stable place in the world sporting landscape. Next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil should provide a dose of rocket fuel to help create even more momentum ahead of 2031. Charting the sport's continued growth is something observers of all stripes will look upon with interest.

title: Del karma a los últimos festejos: cómo le fue a River en Alta Córdoba
description: El equipo de Ponzio visitará un escenario complejo, que incluye una extensa mala racha y dos recientes triunfos en la casa de Instituto.
article_context:
El festejo de Colidio en Alta Córdoba ante Instituto. Foto: Ariel Carreras.
Ante la confirmación de que Instituto no mudará su localía al Mario Alberto Kempes y recibirá a River en el estadio Monumental Presidente Perón, el equipo de Leonardo Ponzio ya sabe que tendrá que jugarse el pase a las semifinales del Clausura en un escenario con mucha historia. En la previa, la excursión al corazón de Alta Córdoba tendrá un fuerte contraste para el Millonario, con un historial general adverso que pesó durante décadas y un presente más alentador que incluye dos alegrías recientes en fila.
Si se toma la película completa de los 14 partidos oficiales que disputó el CARP en ese escenario -10 frente a la Gloria, dos contra Talleres y dos ante Racing de Córdoba-, la estadística global todavía marca números en rojo, con apenas dos victorias, ocho empates y cuatro derrotas. De hecho, durante medio siglo esa cancha fue un auténtico karma para Núñez: entre su primera visita el 24 de noviembre de 1974 (caída 2-1 frente a la T) y la de abril de 1990 , River encadenó 12 presentaciones sin poder ganar ni una sola vez en el tiempo reglamentario , con ocho empates y cuatro tropiezos.
En aquella época esquiva de los años 80, el Millonario sufrió golpes duros en el barrio cordobés: perdió 1-0 con Racing en diciembre de 1982 y padeció dos goleadas frente a Instituto, por 3-0 en noviembre de 1983 y por 4-1 el 8 de marzo de 1987. En el medio, coleccionó empates de todos los colores: 1-1 en 1982, dos 0-0 y un 2-2 a lo largo de 1984, otro 0-0 en febrero de 1988, dos pardas sin goles en 1989 -en la del 5 de marzo ante la Gloria se impuso por 5-4 en la definición por penales que otorgaba un punto extra en aquel certamen- y el 1-1 del 22 de abril de 1990.
Sin embargo, los antecedentes más cercanos cambiaron por completo la ecuación y le hacen un guiño al plantel actual. River acumula seis visitas consecutivas sin conocer la derrota en Alta Córdoba y quebró el maleficio por duplicado en sus últimas dos excursiones, ambas durante 2024 y remontando el resultado.
La primera de esas victorias fue el 15 de abril de 2024, por la última fecha de la Copa de la Liga. Aquella noche, el local arrancó arriba con un gol de penal de Damián Puebla , pero en el segundo tiempo apareció Facundo Colidio con un hat-trick inolvidable para sellar el 3-1 y el boleto a cuartos .
Casi 7 meses más tarde, el 6 de noviembre de 2024 por la Liga Profesional, la historia se repitió en otro partidazo. G regorio Rodríguez abrió la cuenta para la Gloria, Pablo Solari y Paulo Díaz lo dieron vuelta , Jonás Acevedo estampó el 2-2 parcial y, a ocho minutos del cierre, otra vez Colidio -verdugo con cuatro tantos en dos juegos en esa cancha- firmó el 3-2 definitivo tras un gran pase del Pity Martínez. Un antecedente fresco para creer.

headline: River buscará semifinales en Alta Córdoba contra Instituto

title: FA chief signs NDA to view Fifa sell-off plot documents
description: Debbie Hewitt is among several football chiefs to view documents made available by Fifa, but cannot speak about them.
article_context:
Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.
Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.
Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".
Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.
Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'… which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".
They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".
The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.
Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.
"As a member association, the FA is entitled to hold the Fifa president accountable for his actions, and as a Fifa Council vice-president, Hewitt should have seen these plans as soon as they were hatched.
"They had the right to demand to see these documents, and should have exercised that right forcefully and publicly, rather than signing a gagging clause that puts Fifa and Infantino back in control."
115 days, 39 private-jet flights, one election - Infantino's globetrotting
Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.
However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.
It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.
Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.
Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

title: Man Utd's Yoro has Anfield red card overturned
description: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is clear to face Brentford on Saturday as his red card at Anfield is overturned.
article_context:
Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.
Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.
Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.
New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.
"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.
"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."
The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.
However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.
"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.
'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?
How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."
Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.
You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.
The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.
A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.
A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.
It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.
Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.
And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.
Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.
This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.
Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.
Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.
Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.
Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.
An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.
This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.
Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?
Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.
Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca speaks to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Manchester United
United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).
The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.
But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".
"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.
"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.
"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."
United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.
Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.
"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.
"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

title: Video: erró un penal y sus hinchas festejaron porque su clásico rival podía ser campeón
description: En Suecia, la gente de Djurgården celebró remate desviado por Stromland Lien ante Sirius para evitar que Hammarby se encamine a la vuelta olímpica.
article_context:
El fútbol sueco entró en su etapa definitoria, la cual dejó un insólito momento en la Allsvenskan (Primera División). Pasado el fin de semana, una jugada puntual se viralizó por la particularidad que se vivió en el partido entre Sirius y Djurgården, donde un jugador erró un penal y su hinchada empezó a festejar.
Como el Sirius pelea la punta con Hammarby, el clásico rival de Djurgården, los hinchas de la visita celebraron cuando el delantero Kristian Stromland Lien tiró a los 11' del primer tiempo el penal afuera del arco.
Lejos de frustrarse, la tribuna visitante del Estadio Studenternas IP empezó a festejar por esta acción, que hizo que su rival siga con vida y termine ganando por 1-0 para no perderle pisada al Hammarby en la tabla de posiciones.
A falta de una fecha, el Siruis quedó en el segundo puesto con 61 puntos y diferencia de gol de +24 , mientras que el Hammarby terminó primero con 61 unidades y +39 en diferencia de gol.

title: Es oficial: la Copa América 2028 se jugará en los Estados Unidos
description: La Conmebol confirmó que USA volverá a ser sede del torneo continental por tercera vez en su historia. Participarán 16 selecciones, incluyendo seis de la Concacaf.
article_context:
Como había anticipado Olé , este martes se confirmó que la Copa América 2028 se jugará nuevamente en los Estados Unidos. La 49° edición del certamen continental se disputará entre el 9 de junio y el 9 de julio, y participarán 16 selecciones: además de las 10 de Conmebol , dirán presente seis representantes de Concacaf.
De esta manera se confirma que USA será anfitriona del certamen por tercera vez en la historia, después de hacerlo en 2016 (campeón Chile) y 2024 (Argentina). Tras disputar ambas finales, la Argentina buscará el tricampeonato de América.
¡Destino confirmado para la CONMEBOL Copa América 2028! Estados Unidos será el escenario de un nuevo capítulo en la historia del torneo de selecciones más antiguo del planeta. 🏆 pic.twitter.com/MGJLVyIjew
Los detalles relativos a las ciudades anfitrionas, las sedes y el calendario de partidos , así como información adicional sobre los mecanismos de clasificación para las selecciones nacionales de la Concacaf (será según las posiciones en la Copa de Oro 2027), se darán a conocer próximamente.
Alejandro Domínguez, presidente de la Conmebol, confirmó la noticia con un video en sus redes sociales y expresó: "La Copa América es mucho más que un torneo: es parte de nuestra identidad, de nuestra historia y de la grandeza del fútbol sudamericano. En 2028, llevaremos nuevamente esa pasión a los Estados Unidos, reafirmando nuestra histórica alianza con la Concacaf y nuestro compromiso compartido de seguir impulsando el crecimiento del fútbol en todo el continente. Esta nueva edición será una oportunidad más para demostrar que el fútbol no conoce fronteras y que, cuando 'creemos en grande', podemos llegar aún más lejos".
¡La CONMEBOL @CopaAmerica 2028 será en Estados Unidos! ¡El continente vibrará de nuevo con el torneo de selecciones más antiguo del mundo! pic.twitter.com/gvG2UR6qDQ
Por su parte, el presidente de la Concacaf y vicepresidente de la FIFA, Victor Montagliani, señaló: "Nuestra alianza estratégica con la Conmebol refleja el compromiso de nuestra Confederación con el crecimiento del fútbol y con la creación de más oportunidades para nuestras asociaciones miembro y sus selecciones nacionales. Tras nuestra colaboración en 2024, nos complace unir fuerzas nuevamente para traer la Copa América a nuestra región en 2028".
Además agregó: "Este acuerdo brindará a seis selecciones nacionales de la Concacaf una nueva oportunidad de competir contra algunas de las mejores del mundo, al tiempo que refuerza aún más la relevancia competitiva de nuestra Copa Oro de la Concacaf. Esperamos trabajar junto a la Conmebol, las sedes anfitrionas y otras partes clave para organizar un torneo de primer nivel que refleje la pasión, la calidad y el potencial del fútbol en todo el continente".
El comunicado también apunta que "la ampliación de esta alianza estratégica, aprobada por los Consejos de ambas Confederaciones, se fundamenta en la colaboración establecida en 2023, reafirmando el compromiso de crear nuevas oportunidades competitivas para sus selecciones nacionales y de fortalecer el fútbol en todo el continente".

headline: Copa América 2028 se jugará en EE.UU.
caption: La CONMEBOL confirmó que Estados Unidos será la sede de la Copa América 2028, la 49ª edición del torneo continental, que se disputará del 9 de junio al 9 de julio con 16 selecciones, diez de la CONMEBOL y seis de la Concacaf. Será la tercera vez que EE.UU. alberga el certamen, tras 2016 y 2024.

title: No se dan por vencidos: Marruecos irá a la justicia federal para recuperar la Copa Africana de Naciones
description: A través de un comunicado, la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol informó los pasos a seguir luego de que el TAS le devolviera el trofeo a Senegal.
article_context:
La Copa Africana de Naciones se seguirá jugando en los despachos. Al menos, así lo quieren en Marruecos ... Este martes, tras conocerse el fallo del TAS que le devolvió el título a Senegal , la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol emitió un comunicado rechazando la medida y dando a conocer los pasos a seguir en este caso.
Desde la cúpula dirigencial de Los Leones del Atlas pusieron el grito en el cielo al enterarse que debían devolver el título conseguido en enero de este año. Aunque perdieron 1-0 en la final, la CAF (Confederación Africana de Fútbol) les terminó reconociendo el campeonato ya que consideraron que tras el abandono que hizo Senegal, el partido había quedado anulado y el triunfo debía ser 3-0 a favor de Marruecos.
“La Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol expresa su sorpresa y rechazo a que sus solicitudes no hayan sido debidamente consideradas, especialmente en lo relativo a la adopción de las medidas legales necesarias frente a prácticas que vulneran la transparencia y credibilidad del proceso arbitral ”, destacaron en el comunicado.
Además, el documento emitido este martes tras el fallo del TAS tiene dos puntos importantes: advierten que hubo un contacto entre Ulrich Haas, uno de los árbitros de este caso, y la Federación Senegalesa de fútbol , e informaron que no se quedarán de brazos cruzados pese al revés que recibieron. Seguirán en la justicia federal de Suiza ...
“En consecuencia, la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol confirma que utilizará todas las vías legales disponibles para impugnar la decisión del Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte ”, completaron en el comunicado.
La Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol tomó conocimiento de la decisión emitida por el Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte (TAS) el martes 24 de noviembre de 2026 en Lausana, Suiza, respecto al recurso presentado por la Federación Senegalesa de Fútbol contra la decisión de la Confederación Africana de Fútbol (CAF) relacionada con el partido final de la Copa Africana de Naciones 2025.
En este contexto, la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol expresa su sorpresa y rechazo a que sus solicitudes no hayan sido debidamente consideradas, especialmente en lo relativo a la adopción de las medidas legales necesarias frente a prácticas que vulneran la transparencia y credibilidad del proceso arbitral. Particularmente, señala que se confirmó la existencia de contactos entre el árbitro alemán Ulrich Haas y el presidente de la Federación Senegalesa de Fútbol , menos de 48 horas antes de que se emitiera la resolución.
La Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol también señala que la decisión no tomó en consideración la postura ya expresada por organismos internacionales responsables de las normas del fútbol, tanto la FIFA como la propia CAF, respecto de la elegibilidad de los jugadores , sin que ello afectara el resultado del encuentro. Según la federación, esto implica posibles responsabilidades y sanciones disciplinarias .
En consecuencia, la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol confirma que utilizará todas las vías legales disponibles para impugnar la decisión del Tribunal Arbitral del Deporte.
"El Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) ha confirmado la apelación presentada por la Federación Senegalesa de Fútbol (FSF) contra la Confederación Africana de Fútbol (CAF) y la Real Federación Marroquí de Fútbol (FRMF, en francés) en relación con la final de la Copa Africana de Naciones Marruecos 2025 (AFCON 2025). La decisión emitida por la Junta de Apelación de la CAF queda anulada y la decisión de la Junta Disciplinaria de la CAF se restablece . En consecuencia, el resultado obtenido al final de la final de la AFCON 2025 se confirma (1-0 a favor de Senegal)" , indicó el fallo.
Para la Federación Senegalesa de Fútbol, esa determinación no podía ser revisada por los organismos disciplinarios , ya que estaba protegida por la denominada doctrina field of play, que impide cuestionar las decisiones arbitrales tomadas durante un encuentro, salvo que existan pruebas de arbitrariedad o mala fe.
La Federación Real Marroquí de Fútbol, por su parte, sostenía que esa protección no correspondía en este caso. Su argumento era que el abandono momentáneo del campo por parte de los futbolistas senegaleses había representado una infracción de los artículos 82 y 84 del reglamento de la competición, por lo que el árbitro debería haber suspendido definitivamente el partido . En consecuencia, consideraba que el juez había cometido un error de derecho y que su decisión había sido arbitraria.
Sin embargo, el TAS rechazó esa interpretación y entendió que la potestad de reanudar el encuentro o suspenderlo definitivamente correspondía exclusivamente al criterio del árbitro . Al ordenar la continuidad del partido, el juez consideró que estaban dadas las condiciones necesarias, ya que ambos equipos habían regresado al terreno de juego y manifestado su voluntad de continuar. Por ese motivo, el tribunal determinó que su decisión estaba amparada por la doctrina field of play.
Además, el organismo consideró que los artículos 82 y 84 del reglamento de la Copa África no eran aplicables a esta situación. Según explicó, esas disposiciones están destinadas a establecer el resultado de un partido cuando el comportamiento de uno de los equipos lleva al árbitro a decretar su suspensión definitiva, algo que no ocurrió en la final entre Senegal y Marruecos.
El tribunal también reconoció que el árbitro tuvo que tomar su decisión en un contexto de extrema tensión, aunque aclaró que esa circunstancia no alcanzaba para considerar que había actuado de manera arbitraria ni que su criterio había estado condicionado por factores ajenos al juego. De esta manera, concluyó que no había cometido ningún error de derecho. La resolución fue adoptada por unanimidad por los tres integrantes del tribunal.
Por otra parte, el TAS aclaró que las responsabilidades disciplinarias derivadas de lo sucedido ya habían sido abordadas en procedimientos independientes por la CAF. Por ellos habían recibido sanciones la Federación Senegalesa, su entrenador, Pape Thiaw, y algunos futbolistas .

headline: Marruecos acude a justicia suiza por la Copa Africana

title: Klopp advice and Iraola confidence boosts Wirtz
description: Florian Wirtz opens up on why it's the best he has felt since joining Liverpool.
article_context:
Wirtz moved from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool for £116m in 2025
Florian Wirtz says he is enjoying his best form yet at Liverpool and benefiting from Andoni Iraola's confidence and Jurgen Klopp's advice.
Wirtz, 23, scored in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday and has three goals and six assists this season.
The Germany midfielder made the £116m move from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025 and after failing to make his mark in his first campaign in England, is beginning to showcase his quality for Iraola's side.
Speaking in Belgium before Liverpool 's Champions League game against Club Brugge, Wirtz said: "I can't really say that I've changed that much.
"I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it."
He also said he has been picking the brains of Germany manager Klopp, the former Liverpool boss, while on international duty.
"He tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here and tries to give me some advice to get successful over here as he has shown how it is done," Wirtz said.
"He can give me some good advice. It's always small things. More private things.
"But he is speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time."
On the influence of Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool head coach in the summer, Wirtz added: "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football, and I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that.
"I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me."
Liverpool have nine points from their four Champions League games, having won their first three before losing to Fenerbahce in Istanbul this month.
Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are both absent from the travelling squad with injuries, with Iraola confirming that Gakpo will be out for the Merseyside derby this weekend, while adding that it is "difficult to say" for Gravenberch.

title: Un viejo conocido: ¿quién es el delantero de 37 años que busca el Bayern Munich para reemplazar a Harry Kane?
description: El inglés sufrió una lesión en el tobillo izquierdo y estaría cerca de tres meses afuera, por eso los bávaros analizan opciones...
article_context:
El Bayern busca un nuevo delantero (Foto: AFP).
La lesión de Harry Kane encendió las alarmas en el Bayern Munich . El goleador tuvo que abandonar la cancha en el empate 1-1 frente al Colonia por la Bundesliga y los estudios confirmaron una rotura del ligamento de la sindesmosis del tobillo izquierdo. Se estima que el tiempo de recuperación está cerca de los tres meses, por lo que el club ya empezó a buscar alternativas para cubrir su lugar.
Y entre los nombres que aparecieron en el radar bávaro hay uno que llama la atención: Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting . Según informó Sky Sports, el delantero camerunés, nacido en Alemania, es una de las opciones que analiza la dirigencia para reforzar el ataque durante el período en el que Kane estará alejado de las canchas.
El nombre del camerunés de 37 años aparece como una alternativa de experiencia para salir del paso. Entre 2020 y 2024, Eric Choupo-Moting defendió los colores del Bayern sumando un total de 122 apariciones, 38 goles y 11 asistencias , y conoce tanto el club como las exigencias de jugar en uno de los equipos más importantes de Europa.
Actualmente el delantero se encuentra en el New York Red Bulls de Estados Unidos. Además, tiene un punto a favor: su contrato termina en diciembre , cuando finaliza la temporada de la MLS , por lo que podría llegar sin que el club alemán tenga que pagar su pase.
El último ganador del Balón de Oro sufrió una dura lesión durante el empate 1-1 ante el Colonia por la Bundesliga . Sobre la mitad del primer tiempo, Harry Kane tuvo que salir reemplazado. El ex Tottenham duró apenas 20 minutos en cancha. Cuando el goleador se apresuraba para definir, recibió un golpe en la disputa con el defensor rival Joel Schmied .
Los estudios médicos confirmaron una rotura del ligamento de la sindesmosis del tobillo izquierdo , por lo que estaría cerca de tres meses alejado de las canchas, atado a su evolución. La baja representa un problema importante para el equipo dirigido por Vincent Kompany , ya que en los 16 partidos que disputó esta temporada con el Bayern, Kane acumuló 10 goles y 11 asistencias .
Además, Kane no es el único que ocupa la enfermería del equipo alemán. Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Ismael Saibari, Luis Díaz y Alphonso Davies también figuran entre los futbolistas lesionados , mientras que Michael Olise está bajo seguimiento, después de lesionarse en el mismo partido que el inglés.
