headline: Bayern analiza a Choupo-Moting para reemplazar a Kane
caption: El Bayern Munich está considerando al delantero de 37 años Eric Maxim Choupo‑Moting, actualmente en el New York Red Bulls, como opción para cubrir la ausencia de Harry Kane, quien sufrió una rotura del ligamento de la sindesmosis del tobillo izquierdo y se estima que estará fuera unos tres meses. La lesión de Kane se produjo en el empate 1‑1 contra el Colonia en la Bundesliga, lo que ha activado la búsqueda de refuerzos en el ataque del club alemán.

title: La banca del Cholo Simeone a Julián Alvarez: "Los goles seguramente aparecerán"
description: El DT palpitó el encuentro del Atlético de Madrid ante el Viking por la Champions y se refirió al presente de la Araña.
article_context:
Luego de convertirse en el entrenador con más victorias en la historia de LaLiga , Diego Simeone afrontará un nuevo compromiso internacional con el Atlético de Madrid . El conjunto español recibirá este miércoles al Viking de Noruega por la quinta fecha de la fase de liga de la Champions League , donde apenas cosechó cuatro puntos de los 12 posibles.
En la antesala del encuentro, el Cholo brindó una conferencia de prensa en la que, entre otras cuestiones, volvió a referirse al presente de Julián Álvarez . "Son futbolistas con gol y seguramente aparecerán" , sostuvo el entrenador al ser consultado por el rendimiento de sus delanteros.
Una de las particularidades del Aleti en este tramo de la temporada pasa por la escasa contundencia de sus atacantes y el aporte goleador de futbolistas de otras posiciones. Sin embargo, el argentino no se mostró preocupado por la procedencia de los tantos.
"El gol necesita llegar de una u otra manera relacionado a lo que el equipo propone", explicó. Y agregó: "Salvo David, que ha tenido tres goles, obviamente esperamos a Julián, a Sorloth, a Lookman cuando se recupere" .
En esa misma línea se había manifestado el pasado domingo, tras el triunfo por 3-0 ante el Getafe que le permitió alcanzar las 345 victorias en el campeonato español. En aquella oportunidad, Simeone valoró la actuación de la Araña más allá de su efectividad frente al arco: "Lo necesitamos, hizo un partido bárbaro, se asoció con todos y el gol llegará cuando tenga que llegar" .
🗣️ SIMEONE, SOBRE JULIÁN: "LE VAMOS A EXIGIR, CLARAMENTE, PORQUE LO TIENE" ⚽ "El gol llegará cuando tenga que llegar" ⏳ "Acá estamos para esperar" 🎯 "Ha hecho siempre goles importantes" #Simeone #JuliánÁlvarez #Atleti pic.twitter.com/gAHMb6FHgK
El enfrentamiento entre españoles y noruegos da lugar a una coincidencia peculiar: ambos llegarán al encuentro con la misma cantidad de puntos (4) . Con la mitad de la fase de liga por delante, el equipo madrileño buscará aprovechar la localía para acercarse a los puestos de clasificación directa a octavos de final.
Simeone hizo especial hincapié en la intensidad del conjunto noruego, su capacidad para presionar y el peligro que representa en las acciones de pelota parada. "Nosotros jugamos en casa y tendremos que intentar aprovechar esa situación con nuestra gente" , señaló el Cholo.
Respecto a las aspiraciones del Atlético en la competición, añadió: "Quedan cuatro partidos todavía, quedan doce puntos en juego, necesitamos sumar lo máximo posible y, si no es entrar entre los ocho primeros, en el lugar que nos toque, lo más arriba siempre mejor ".

headline: Simeone confía en Julián Álvarez

title: La historia que compartió Ponzio luego de la victoria de River y su fuerte conferencia
description: El entrenador manifestó sus ganas de seguir siendo entrenador del Millonario en 2027 y ya piensa en Instituto.
article_context:
Mientras el plantel profesional disfruta de este martes de jornada libre luego de los trabajos regenerativos realizados en el primer día de la semana en Ezeiza, en River ya se palpita el cruce con Instituto en Alta Córdoba por los cuartos del Clausura. Y en medio de esa calma previa, Leonardo Ponzio volvió a mostrarse activo en las redes tal como solía hacerlo cuando todavía no era entrenador interino. Así, después de haber manifestado públicamente sus ganas de seguir en el cargo en 2027 , el DT compartió en su cuenta de Instagram una historia oficial del club con el vlog de los hinchas en el Monumental durante el 3-1 sobre Lanús.
El reposteo del León, que incluye el cantito "esta hinchada se merece ser campeón" está lejos de ser casual teniendo en cuenta el reconocimiento habitual que tiene hacia la gente. De hecho, apenas consumada la importante victoria frente al Granate, no dudó en destacar el respaldo recibido en una noche repleta de tensión: "El partido fue el que fuimos a buscar. Y la gente tiene un párrafo aparte: nos aguantó, y la necesidad de ellos es la nuestra. Como digo siempre, en hincha es la historia de este club", empatizó con los 85.000 hinchas que coparon el Monumental y pidieron a gritos por el título.
En lo futbolístico, el entrenador retomará las prácticas este miércoles por la mañana en Ezeiza y comenzará a planificar el partido ante la Gloria, a la espera de saber cómo evolucionarán Marcos Acuña -salió a los 12 minutos del segundo tiempo frente a Lanús por una molestia en el aductor izquierdo- y Lucas Beltrán -reemplazado cinco minutos por un traumatismo en el tobillo derecho tras chocar con el arquero rival-. Ninguno de los dos necesitó estudios médicos y por el momento serán evaluados día a día , mientras que también Ponzio sigue muy pendiente de la evolución de Fausto Vera , quien se recupera de una tendinitis posterior al desgarro.
El guiño en redes llega horas después de la conferencia en la que Ponzio marcó la cancha con firmeza sobre sus ganas de dejar de ser interino en el próximo año y seguir en el cargo en medio del ruido por Ramón Díaz. "Me encuentra en una edad para meterle con todo. Por supuesto que quiero ser entrenador de River. Lo tengo clarísimo. Sigo insistiendo porque creo que me gané el lugar, soy sincero", afirmó el DT.
Además, sin nombrarlo, lanzó un tiro por elevación ante los coqueteos del Pelado y su hijo Emiliano: "Parece que este lugar se está vendiendo u ofreciendo y no tenemos que ir por ese lado. Cuando hay alguien en ese lado hay que respetarlo. Sé de qué lado viene: los conozco a todos. Lo que me molesta es que le hagamos mal al club, a nuestros jugadores". Con la banca del hincha que tanto lo aplaudió y lo reconoció en sus tiempos como jugador, el León defiende su silla en Núñez...
Ponzio habló sobre el estilo de juego que busca implementar y su rol al frente de River en este segundo semestre de 2026.

headline: Ponzio celebra victoria 3-1 y confirma continuidad en River 2027
caption: Tras el triunfo 3-1 de River sobre Lanús, el entrenador Leonardo Ponzio repostó en Instagram la historia oficial del club y, en una conferencia, reiteró su intención de seguir al frente del Millonario hasta 2027, señalando que ya piensa en el próximo cruce contra Instituto en los cuartos del Clausura. title: 'I miss being on court' - Sinner has 'minor surgery' on knee
description: World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.
article_context:
Jannik Sinner attended a ceremony for players who had become world number one at the ATP Finals in Turin
World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.
The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.
In a post on Instagram, Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee.
"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," the 25-year-old wrote.
"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped.
"I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."
Earlier in November, Sinner said his goal was to go to Australia and potentially "play a few tournaments" before the first Grand Slam of the year begins on 17 January.
However, the Italian has also stressed the need to think of his long-term career in protecting his body.
The Instagram post is the first time Sinner has specified what the knee issue is.
In a video posted on his Youtube channel in October, Sinner said he had also lost "a lot of weight" after having his tonsils removed.
He also described having "days where I felt nothing and could play without any problems, and then days where I couldn't move at all".
He suffered a nasty fall in the first match of his Wimbledon title defence and also had blood seeping through his shoes because of a problematic toenail.
Alexander Zverev has become world number one in Sinner's absence, while rival Carlos Alcaraz swept four titles after returning from his injury lay-off in September.
Sinner comes from behind to retain Wimbledon title against Zverev
Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches.
He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters' , and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way.
However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title.
Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece.
He ended his season in early October , meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025.
Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking.
Having met in three of the four Grand Slam finals last year, Sinner and Alcaraz played each other only once in 2026.
Sinner won their final at the Monte Carlo Masters shortly before Alcaraz spent four months out with a wrist injury.
Alcaraz's victory at the season-ending ATP Finals means he is only 350 ranking points behind Sinner - although the Spaniard will be defending 2,000 of those at the Australian Open.
"It's a shame we don't have Jannik," Alcaraz told SuperTennis TV , external after winning the ATP Finals on Sunday.
"We really miss him. I have not seen him for many months right now since I got injured in April.
"I can't wait to see him fit, healthy. I am pretty sure that he is going to come back even better and stronger."
Alcaraz will be the defending champion in Melbourne, having beaten Djokovic to complete a historic career Grand Slam in January.

title: Why the Premier League's set-piece goals dried up -- and why Arsenal are still No. 1 anyway
description: Arsenal won the Premier League in controversial fashion last season, but the set-piece goals they counted on have disappeared. Why?
article_context:
Last season, Arsenal scored 19 goals from corner kicks en route to winning their first Premier League title in over 20 years.
You know this because it's all we talked about. And it's all we talked about because (1) Arsenal are one of the most popular sports teams on the planet, and (2) everyone else started doing it, too. It became, increasingly, soccer without the soccer .
From one side, bad-faith commentators tried to make it sound like Arsenal's title wasn't worth as much as teams that attacked more aggressively. From the other side, bad-faith commentators acted confused that neutrals didn't enjoy watching a defensive team whose matches featured less ball-in-play time than anyone else in the league.
In the middle: it seemed like modern soccer had reached an inflection point, where a sudden leaguewide strategic shift -- led by the best team in England and one of the three or four best teams in the world -- had made the game worse to watch. That is, if you liked watching things like "passing" and "open-play goals" -- all of them had fallen off a cliff.
Given the vastly different punishments for infractions during a corner kick -- a penalty if a defender is too aggressive, a free kick 100 yards away from goal if the attacker is too aggressive -- teams realized there was little downside to creating what the analyst Michael Caley called a "meat wall" in front of the opposition goalkeeper and grappling for space inside the six-yard box. Teams also seemed to decide, collectively, that there was little upside in taking risks in the other phases of the game.
Had this been the way soccer always worked, then, well, soccer probably never would've become the most popular sport in the world. But any rule-change adopted by the Premier League to make it harder to score from corners would, in a way, be a direct punishment of Arsenal since they drove the shift and they benefitted from it more than anyone.
The Gunners scored just 42 goals from open-play last season and won the title by scoring the most corner kick goals in a season from any Premier League team ever.
With FIFA advising their referees to crack down on penalty-area physicality at the World Cup over the summer, it seemed like set pieces would once again be the story of the Premier League season -- in one way or another.
Well, 11 games into the 2026-27 season, Arsenal have scored just one goal from corner kicks. And Arsenal ... are sitting atop the standings, a full six points clear of second place.
- Predicting the Premier League season now: How all 20 teams will finish - Man United need January help to avoid Premier League relegation - How fallen giants and fans bounce back from scandal and relegation
Ahead of this season, the Premier League didn't make any rule changes but instead instructed its referees to focus on "non-footballing holding actions that have no place on the football pitch." This included things like a player not even looking at the ball as he made contact with an opponent or a player making contact with an opponent while not even attempting to make a play on the ball.
These vague directives can often be quite powerful. In 2019, the NFL told refs to stop calling so many holding penalties , the number of holding penalties nearly halved overnight, and it was suddenly easier for offenses to move the ball down the field.
And what do you know? Premier League refs were told to call more fouls during corner kicks, and they are calling more fouls during corner kicks.
Per a study recently conducted by Caley : "Attackers have been called for 5.8 fouls for every 100 corners this season, up from 4.6 last season," It's being driven, in particular, by an increase in fouls suffered by goalkeepers: 3.1 per 100 corners this season, up from 2.5 last season and an average of 1.8 in the five seasons prior.
What happened last season, basically, was that teams packed the six-yard box and then smashed in-swinging corners into that area. In-swingers are much easier to score from because they just require a slight redirection, because they're already headed toward the goal, and because they lead to closer chances to goal than outswingers. Their effectiveness is theoretically canceled out, though, because it's also easier for the goalkeeper to catch them.
The rise in set-piece scoring last season was, essentially, driven by teams realizing there was a way you could hit in-swinging corners and prevent goalkeepers from claiming them. But the increase in foul-calling this season seems to have totally halted the trend.
Goalkeeper claims fell to 3.1 per 100 corners taken as crosses last season. This happened even as corner deliveries increasingly targeted areas in the six-yard box where keepers are the most likely to be able to claim the ball. I created a model to predict claims based on where crosses landed, and this model predicted that goalkeepers would be able to catch far more than they actually did, about 7.6 out of every 100 corner crosses. This season the number of claims has nearly doubled, up to 5.6. Punches have been rising, and even continued that trajectory in 2026-27 despite the increase in claims. All told, goalkeepers are now reaching over 15 percent of corner kick crosses.
All of this, unsurprisingly, has tanked the number of goals being scored from corner kicks. The turnaround is remarkable:
We've shifted from one extreme to the other over the course of a single off season. Last season had the highest corner-kick-goal rate of any in the Opta database. This season has the lowest .
In a sense: yes. We're not talking about how the quality of play is terrible and how we only see set-piece goals anymore. Even with new tactics reshaping the game , the on-field product definitely feels better this season.
But the massive decline in corner-kick goals is likely also a small-sample-size fluke. "While goals from corner kicks have fallen by about 40 percent, [expected goals] from corners has dropped by only about 10 percent," Caley found. "At about 4.4 xG per 100 corners, this season ranks second among Premier League seasons in the last 15 years."
Now, xG (expected goals) from corner kicks is significantly harder to measure -- little nudges from defenders or an inch on an attacker's head can drastically influence the difficulty of a chance, and those things won't be picked up by an xG model. But through 11 games, Premier League teams have scored 29 goals from corners, while they'd be expected to score 42 (41.97).

title: Liverpool's Wirtz: Iraola is bringing me back to my best
description: Florian Wirtz has credited head coach Andoni Iraola with helping him to find his best form for Liverpool in almost two years.
article_context:
BRUGES, Belgium -- Liverpool attacker Florian Wirtz has credited head coach Andoni Iraola with helping him to find his best form in almost two years but said he has "always believed" in his own abilities.
Wirtz was the standout performer in Liverpool's 4-0 victory over Manchester United on Sunday, registering a goal and an assist as well as creating 10 chances in open play -- the most by a player in a Premier League match for more than a decade.
His impressive display comes amid a productive run for both club and country, with the Germany international having managed 11 goal contributions in his last 15 games in all competitions.
Wirtz and Liverpool will look to build on their big win against United when they face Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Asked in a news conference ahead of the match if he is enjoying his best spell in a Liverpool shirt, Wirtz replied: "Probably yes. "I think in the last few games I got a lot of goal contributions and I think you could say that I am in the best form since I arrived.
"To be honest, I cannot really say that I have changed much. I think that I have become a bit better on a physical level. That is the only reason I could explain it, but I also started to know better the English football and the league. And at the moment I am feeling very good. I am enjoying my football at Liverpool. I am happy it is going like this at the moment."
Reflecting on his relationship with Iraola, Wirtz added: "I am really enjoying playing under him. He is a really good coach. He has shown that his whole career as a manager. He is bringing me back into the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football.
"I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me. I am really happy with that."
Wirtz has faced intense scrutiny since joining Liverpool in a £116 million ($152.1m) move from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. The 23-year-old endured an underwhelming debut season at Anfield but he insists he has never lost faith in his own abilities.
"It's mainly a thing that goes on in my own head."
"It's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself. I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities and I know them now. Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I'm just enjoying the moment and really happy at the moment that it's going well. I'm happy with myself and I want to continue like that."
Wirtz has also benefitted from the appointment of Jürgen Klopp as Germany boss, with the former Liverpool manager having spoken at length with the midfielder about what is expected at Anfield.
"We speak always about Liverpool when we have the time to do so," Wirtz said. "He had a great time here. He is the coach who stayed here the most of his career. He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to get successful over here because he has shown how it is done.
"It is really good that he knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here, he can give me some good advice."
headline: Florian Wirtz agradece a Iraola su mejor forma
caption: El atacante del Liverpool, Florian Wirtz, declaró que el entrenador Andoni Iraola le ha devuelto la confianza y lo ha llevado a su mejor nivel en casi dos años. Tras protagonizar la victoria 4‑0 ante el Manchester United con gol, asistencia y diez ocasiones creadas, Wirtz busca mantener la racha en el próximo duelo contra el Club Brugge en la Champions League.

title: Should you trade Davion Mitchell? Move on from De'Aaron Fox?
description: Steve Alexander looks at three players on the rise and three who are slumping and how fantasy managers should react.
article_context:
Davion Mitchell is turning heads and leading the league in assists, Quentin Grimes is on a heater in Los Angeles and Cedric Coward is quickly emerging as a fantasy force. All are moving up the fantasy rankings.
Meanwhile, Kel'el Ware 's stint for the 1-16 Bucks has been a nightmare, Jalen Green is not pulling his weight in Phoenix and De'Aaron Fox has really struggled in San Antonio. Which ones should you move on from at this point?
Risers and Fallers helps you track hot players who are worth holding onto, players are are likely overvalued right now (see the final paragraph under Risers), as well as struggling players you might be better off without. Here's more on each of these players.
Resources: Rankings | Adds/Drops | Scoring leaders | Player Rater | Mock draft lobby | Depth charts | Schedule | Injuries
Mitchell was drafted around the 10th round in most of my 12-team drafts and he's shocking the world, leading the league in assists and appearing to love playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo . His November numbers include 17.5 points, 8.9 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.7 blocks and 2.7 triples, while hitting 52.6% of his shots.
This might seem to scream "trade him before the bottom falls out," but I don't think that's the case. You likely drafted him very late in your draft (or even got him off the waiver wire) and he's also been one of your best players all season. Especially over the last two weeks, when he's been a Top 10 fantasy player. I'm holding onto Mitchell until further notice and I think he's very driven to win the assist title this season. And with guys like Bam Adebayo and Giannis to throw it to, he should continue to do this all year. Ride the wave.
I sadly wrote that Sandro Mamukelashvili was a Riser last week, but things have changed a lot since then. Grimes has been on fire with Austin Reaves (heel) and Luka Doncic (rest) missing games, but that's not the main reason he's cooking right now.
He scored 22 points last Sunday and then exploded for a career-high 47 against Charlotte on Tuesday. He then scored 20 and 13 points in each of his last two games and is averaging a ridiculous 25.5 points, 5.0 3-pointers, 6.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists over his last four.
Sure, he'll take a hit once Reaves is back, but the Lakers are going to be careful with Reaves and we've already seen them give Luka and Walker Kessler the occasional night off. But the most important point here is that I suspect Luka has figured out the Lakers are a better team when Grimes is cooking, and he's become his new go-to guy after Reaves and Kessler, shoving Mamukelashvili out of the way. And that means that Grimes should be a solid fantasy player all season. If you've got him, hang onto him rather than trying to capitalize on his recent success. Hopefully, he's just getting started.
Coward is becoming a force and reminds me a little of Dylan Harper , who's out with a hip injury right now for the Spurs. Going into Saturday's game, Coward was coming off a fun four-game run that resulted in 20 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 1.5 steals, 1.0 blocks and 3.8 3-pointers with excellent shooting from everywhere.
He's been playing well all year and while I knew he was an intriguing prospect, I didn't expect him to be this good this fast. He's also a big reason the Grizzlies are 12-5 (along with Ty Jerome , Cameron Boozer and Cam Spencer ) and they're going to continue to build the team around him (and Boozer) going forward. The Grizzlies want to make the playoffs and do some damage while they're there, and Coward is going to be a force for the rest of the season, assuming he stays healthy.
If you're looking for some hot players to deal while their trade value is high, James Harden (out of his mind on Friday), Franz Wagner (before Paolo Banchero returns), Anthony Davis (before he gets hurt) and Klay Thompson (before he runs out of gas) probably fit the bill.
Ware's minutes have been highly inconsistent and he's been one of the more disappointing players I drafted this year. And, unfortunately, that was in a ton of leagues. I'm not giving up hope just yet, as there's still a chance the Bucks will eventually give up on the season and start developing their young players. And Ware's ability to score, board, steal, block and shoot the 3-pointer is nothing to sneeze at.
Despite a 50-point explosion from Tyler Herro on Saturday, they still lost to the Sixers and are now 1-16 on the season. I really don't understand the point of running Kyle Kuzma , Myles Turner and Herro out there for 35 minutes every night when young players like Ware, Brayden Burries , Ryan Rollins and Kasparas Jakucionis need some of those minutes. If your league is 10 teams or less, Ware might be droppable. But in 12-team leagues, I'm still hanging onto Ware, who had six points, eight boards, a steal and a block on Saturday. That said, if things are still going like this in a month, I might have to check out.
I think Green is fine to hold in leagues that are 14-teams and larger, but he's droppable in 12-team leagues, and is especially not worth having in smaller ones (10 or eight teams, etc.). He has the ability to be an elite scorer, but is averaging just 12.5 points on the season, is shooting fantasy teams into oblivion with his 41.8% from the field and 70.5% from the line, and is at just 0.9 steals, 0.4 blocks and 1.2 3-pointers.
Green may get traded, but either way, it feels like the Suns are either looking for a true point guard ( Dejounte Murray ?) or may just start rolling with Collin Gillespie . The bottom line is that his name is bigger than his game and I'm not sure Green's ever going to become a fantasy must-have player. And, so far, he's barely even worth rostering this year, if at all.
There's still time to join or create a league in the No. 1 fantasy basketball game. Your league starts fresh on the first scoring period following completion of your draft.
I'm not sure what's going on with Fox, but entering Saturday night, he was averaging just 10.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.7 3-pointers on 40% shooting. And in his three games before that, those numbers dipped even further, including zero 3-pointers made and 29% shooting. Then he scored just five points on Saturday.
Add in the fact that he didn't see a boost after Harper (hip) went down, and this is another concern. The Spurs are deep, Harper and Stephon Castle have a high usage rate (not to mention Victor Wembanyama ), and Fox is basically just a facilitator o
headline: Mitchell lidera en asistencias
caption: Davion Mitchell lidera la liga en asistencias y ha sido uno de los mejores jugadores de la temporada, por lo que se recomienda retenerlo en lugar de tratar de comerciarlo. title: Karabell's fantasy notebook: Was Paul George this season's biggest draft-day steal?
description: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA and what it means for fantasy.
article_context:
When the Boston Celtics stunningly traded star SF/SG Jaylen Brown to the rival Philadelphia 76ers this past summer, Celtics fans groaned not only about losing a key 10-year veteran who averaged 28.7 PPG last season, but about the once-great SF/PF Paul George joining the roster as his replacement. Meanwhile, 76ers fans mightily celebrated George leaving it.
Was all that fair? Probably not, especially in retrospect, because we are in the seventh week of the NBA season with Brown and George performing at a similar statistical level, with George well ahead on the Player Rater (No. 42 to No. 75) and averaging 39.5 ESPN fantasy points per game, just a bit ahead of Brown at 38.5 points. Who would have expected this development?
Let's focus not on Brown, who is doing precisely what the 76ers expected him to do in a star-filled lineup, averaging 22.4 PPG in 34.3 MPG, but on George, who has been a solid fit for Boston's aggressive 3-point field goal attack. George, 36 and averaging 19.9 PPG in 30.1 MPG, rested for Sunday night's road game versus the Golden State Warriors (which the Celtics lost!), but this tragic figure, who participated in only 78 of a possible 164 games during two disappointing 76ers seasons, has missed only three games this season -- just like Brown.
Durability was likely the biggest concern for fantasy managers potentially interested in George, which is why he fell to Round 7, at least, in ESPN average live drafts. Most fantasy managers probably looked at Brown's lofty numbers from last season (achieved sans injured teammate Jayson Tatum ) and could not wait to invest among the first 30 selections. Still, one could see a path to similar production if the games were similar . We can check back on comparing these fellows in a month and, who knows, perhaps George is hurt again tomorrow, and the entire premise was silly. Then again, perhaps not.
There's still time to join or create a league in the No. 1 fantasy basketball game. Your league starts fresh on the first scoring period following completion of your draft.
The Celtics keep George's minutes in check, and more than half his attempted field goals are from 3-point range. He's hitting 40.7% on 3-pointers. George is also fourth in the NBA in steals per game , such a critical differentiator in roto formats. His three missed games each came during the second half of back-to-back outings, and we should expect that continues. That's fine, really, hardly atypical behavior for veterans in this league. If it keeps George healthy for 65 games, a figure he has reached in one of the past seven seasons, we are all for it. Give George credit. He was caught in an awkward situation, but these numbers are solid.
Ultimately, even though production and health are similar today , it is hard to make a great case to trade Brown for George in a points format or a roto/categories league, but it isn't nearly as wild a thought as it was when this real-life trade occurred, or even two months ago. One of these fellows is, predictably, not earning great value from his fantasy draft-day status . The other has been, well, a steal.
headline: Paul George, posible robo
caption: Paul George ha sido una sólida adquisición para los Celtics, promediando 19.9 puntos por partido y liderando en robos de balón. Su desempeño ha sido similar al de Jaylen Brown, lo que lo convierte en una posible ganga en el draft de fantasy.

title: Another U.S.-held Copa América is great for USMNT but not South America
description: For the third time in 12 years, the Copa América will be held in the U.S. That's exciting for the USMNT but it robs South America of the game it loves.
article_context:
The Copa América is returning to the U.S. in 2028 , the third time in the past four editions that South America's premier international tournament will take place in North America. It will be the second straight edition of the competition to be held stateside, while the centenary-celebration tournament was hosted by the U.S. in 2016.
Is that too much time for a continental competition to be held outside its own continent? And what kind of an opportunity does it present for the hosts, the U.S. men's national team , bang in the middle of the four-year cycle building to the 2030 FIFA World Cup ?
To answer those questions, ESPN turned to Jeff Carlisle and Tim Vickery.
The Copa América is returning to the United States, and that counts as great news for the U.S. men's national team.
The USMNT has at times struggled to fill out its schedule with quality opponents. Part of that is down to the top-heavy nature of Concacaf. As things stand, Canada , Mexico and Panama can provide the U.S. with a consistent challenge. From there, the standard falls significantly.
The international calendar does the USMNT no favors either. The biennial nature of the Gold Cup means that two out of the three summers in a World Cup cycle are dominated with matches against Concacaf opponents. World Cup qualifying and the Concacaf Nations League make the schedule even more Concacaf-centric. Elsewhere, international windows are often clogged with qualifying for continental competitions or other versions of the Nations League, restricting the availability of teams to play friendlies.
The Copa América offers a welcome dose of variety and quality. The U.S. invariably faces teams with which it isn't as familiar, and there is the potential to face some of the hemisphere's most accomplished sides like Argentina and Brazil . The fact that the USMNT failed to make it out of the group stage in the 2024 edition of the Copa -- yes, that included a defeat to Panama -- only reinforces the point that it can benefit from being tested in a tournament setting.
The benefits to the U.S. from hosting Copa América are enhanced given that the USMNT finds itself in a period of transition. Not only is the search on for a new manager, but a new generation of players has taken its first steps into the international arena. Time will be needed for coach and players to adapt and get to know each other. The Copa América is the perfect setting to test which players and tactics will suit the USMNT best going forward.
One minor complication is the fact that the U.S. will also be hosting the Olympic Games in 2028. This isn't to suggest that the Olympics are at all on par with the Copa América. In terms of soccer, the latter dwarfs the former in terms of prestige, but the Olympics garner a significant amount of attention in the U.S. As such, U.S. Soccer has placed an emphasis on performing well in the competition, hiring former LAFC manager Steve Cherundolo to coach what will be primarily a U23 team. Given the impressive starts with the USMNT by the likes of Red Bull New York 's Julian Hall and the Philadelphia Union 's Cavan Sullivan , the full national team may end up cannibalizing the Olympic team to a degree.
That said, such a dilemma is a champagne problem. Tournament experience, no matter where it happens, is a valuable resource when the big stage of a World Cup comes around. The Copa América will no doubt benefit the USMNT in that regard. -- Carlisle
South America boasts the oldest continental competition in the world, but its history has been checkered and uneven. First played in 1916 and held on an annual basis at the start, the Copa América had fallen into disuse by the early 1980s, but then it was brought back in 1987. Two developments were key to its revival: instead of dictatorships snarling at each other, democratic regimes were returning to the region; and football as a televised spectacle was by this point making advances, with new powerful forces such as cable on the horizon.
And so, initially on a two-year basis, the tournament went all around the continent -- in some places ( Paraguay in 1999, Colombia in 2001, Venezuela in 2007) for the first time. Fresh frontiers were explored even in places where the competition had been held before; 2004 in Peru , for example, was the first time the Copa moved outside the capital city of Lima. This process was important. There was an undoubted feel-good factor, a boost to national morale, in those places that were hosting the show for the first time. And it was also a boost to the construction of new stadiums.
But CONMEBOL now seem to have turned their backs on the idea. After 1987, the Copa did its tour of all ten of its nations, and then set off on a second lap in Argentina in 2011. But after Argentina, Chile and Brazil, the process has stalled. Ecuador were next in line -- and are still waiting, because the tournament keeps coming back to the United States.
Herculez Gomez and Alejandro Moreno debate the biggest storylines and break down the best highlights that soccer in the Americas has to offer. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only)
The first time seemed to be a one off. In 2016, CONMEBOL bizarrely staged the centenary tournament outside its own borders, the justification being that the U.S. was well equipped to do a bigger version of the competition. Since 1993, it had been the custom to invite two teams from outside South America to make the number of competitors 12. Japan and Qatar have both been invited, but normally the invitees are from Concacaf. And so, instead of two extra Concacaf nations, the 2016 version had six, making the Copa bigger -- and more lucrative.
There was a repeat in 2024, this time sold as an important part of the U.S.'s preparations to stage this year's World Cup, and a chance for the South Americans to have some match practice in the conditions.
The decision to send 2028 up north has only one justification: money. The USA has plenty of large-capacity stadiums, and CONMEBOL have also been seduced by the cultural tradition of selling tickets using dynamic pricing. "Football needs resources," is the often used line, although the morality of extracting ever larger amounts from committed fans is surely open to debate.
And there is another debate to be had. This means that, in a 12-year period, South America's international tournament will only have been played in the U.S. and in Brazil. True, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay have a game each in the next World Cup, but that i

title: Sinner abandons treatment on right knee to have it surgically repaired
description: Jannik Sinner has undergone a "minor" operation on his bothersome right knee after it didn't respond well enough to other treatments, the Italian tennis star said Tuesday.
article_context:
MONACO -- Jannik Sinner has undergone a "minor" operation on his bothersome right knee after it didn't respond well enough to other treatments, the Italian tennis star said Tuesday.
Sinner hasn't played since defending his Wimbledon title in July for his fifth Grand Slam trophy and recently lost the No. 1 ranking to Alexander Zverev .
"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," Sinner wrote on Instagram. "After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."
He did not say when he expects to return to return to the court but had already announced that he was done playing for the season.
"I have to respect the protocols at the moment because if we rush things we could have more serious problems," Sinner said during a news conference in Milan this month.
When Sinner shut down his season last month, a statement from his management team said he "will follow a course of treatment for inflammation in his knee."
It's the second prolonged absence from the tennis tour in two years after Sinner accepted a three-month ban in a settlement with the World Anti-Doping Agency for a doping case in 2025.
The Australian Open, the first Grand Slam of 2027, starts Jan. 17. It could mark the second straight Grand Slam that Sinner sits out after also missing the US Open.
The French Open, the year's second Slam, starts in late May.
headline: Sinner se somete a cirugía en rodilla
caption: El tenista italiano Jannik Sinner se sometió a una operación menor en su rodilla derecha después de que no respondiera bien a otros tratamientos. Sinner ha estado ausente de las canchas desde que defendió su título en Wimbledon en julio y perdió el ranking número uno ante Alexander Zverev.

title: Jadson Viera: del "que las críticas caigan en mí" al "dejar a Independiente en lo más alto"
description: Ya con la mente puesta en Vélez, el entrenador del Rojo analizó a su próximo rival, el momento del equipo y los objetivos que tiene por delante. Mirá qué dijo.
article_context:
Jadson Viera buscará estirar su estadía en el club ante el Fortín. (Foto: Prensa Independiente).
Jadson Viera ya dio vuelta la página, dejó atrás la victoria ante Argentinos Juniors y piensa en el duelo de los cuartos de final del Torneo Clausura ante Vélez . El entrenador, que logró estirar su estadía en el club, analizó al rival de la próxima instancia, el momento que se encuentra atravesando el equipo, los juveniles y más.
El uruguayo calificó al Fortín como un conjunto que "juega muy bien" , sostuvo que es "mucho más vertical" que el Bicho y dio algunos indicios de sus facetas. "Te ataca entre líneas directamente, con un poco menos de posesión. Es un equipo duro que trata de presionarte mucho todo el tiempo", dejó en claro este martes por la tarde en diálogo con TyC Sports.
Con el triunfo en La Paternal , el Rojo volvió a evidenciar que le sienta bien jugar fuera del Libertadores de América-Ricardo Enrique Bochini , donde apenas logró dos victorias en todo el segundo semestre y sintió la presión de los hinchas. "Saben que nosotros somos duros de visitante. Vamos a tratar de aprovechar algún espacio. Seguramente, para los dos, sobre el final del partido los juveniles pueden llegar a hacer la diferencia", dijo el charrúa.
Viera afirmó que "estamos ilusionados" con la posibilidad de dar pelea en el campeonato , blanqueó que a su Independiente le queda "cómodo el partido a partido" y que "está todo muy parejo" en el fútbol argentino. "Hay que pensar en el partido que viene y que la ilusión vaya en función de lo que pasó con Argentinos y lo que pase con Vélez", continuó.
Consciente de que está en el blanco de los hinchas por la irregularidad del equipo, Jadson expresó que "trato de no mirar mucho", aunque confesó que prefiere que "las críticas" le caigan a él y "no a los jugadores" . La tensión por el clima electoral se sintió en cada encuentro que Independiente jugó en su cancha, uno de los ejes fundamentales por los malos resultados en el LdA-REB. "No es fácil estar en esta etapa. Quiero dejar al club lo más alto posible", afirmó.
Y agregó: "El grupo me abrazó desde el primer día que llegamos. Yo voy a seguir para adelante como desde el primer día que llegué. No tenemos un gran plantel . Reducido, sí, de juveniles, pero con eso vamos a seguir trabajando".
-"Cuando llegué le dije que quería que sea el Maxi Meza que yo conozco. Le encontré una función de libertad en la parte ofensiva, con algo de compromiso en la defensiva. Nos da muchos movimientos, nos da la pausa, el balón parado, el gol".
-"Hablé con Rodrigo Rey abiertamente, le comenté un poco mi pensar. Estoy agradecido con él. Es un referente, un capitán que siempre nos está ayudando en lo que sea. Hay una buena unión. Obviamente que son decisiones y lo entendió bien y sigue tirando para adelante como loco".
-"Me gusta la localía, que la gente pueda apoyarnos. Este último tiempo nos ha costado un poco de local. Este momento de los playoffs hubiera sido diferente. También resulta que somos un equipo duro de visitante".

headline: Jadson Viera quiere dejar a Independiente en la cima
caption: El entrenador uruguayo de Independiente, Jadón Viera, declaró que prefiere que las críticas recae en él y no en los jugadores, y que su objetivo es concluir su etapa en el club “lo más alto posible”. Con la vista puesta en el próximo duelo de cuartos de final del Torneo Clausura contra Vélez, analizó al rival y resaltó la fortaleza del equipo como visitante, mientras reconoce la necesidad de los juveniles para marcar la diferencia.

title: Florian Wirtz hails Iraola and Klopp as he reaches new levels for Liverpool
description: Playmaker in best form since moving to Anfield ‘I am really enjoying playing under Iraola’ Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025. The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Mancheste

caption: El mediocampista alemán Florian Wirtz agradeció a Andoni Iraola el papel clave en su recuperación de forma, describiendo que bajo su dirección está disfrutando más y ha alcanzado su mejor nivel en Liverpool. Tras una temporada debut complicada bajo Arne Slot, Wirtz anotó un gol improvisado en la victoria 4-0 del equipo.

title: Wolves' DiVincenzo cleared for basketball activities
description: The Timberwolves said Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for basketball activities after Achilles surgery.
article_context:
The Minnesota Timberwolves could be getting some help soon. Anthony Edwards is still out, but Donte DiVincenzo is getting closer to returning. Shams Charania reports that he is targeting around New Year's to make his season debut.
The guard tore his Achilles tendon in Game 4 of the Wolves' first-round series against the Nuggets last April. He had surgery on April 26.
The team issued a statement Tuesday saying that he's been cleared for basketball activities and is progressing toward a return to play.
Edwards had knee surgery last month. There is no firm timetable for his return.
Without him, Minnesota has stayed afloat thanks to new addition LaMelo Ball . The Wolves are 13-5 and in third place in the West.
DiVincenzo played in all 82 regular-season games last season, averaging 12 points, four rebounds and four assists per game.
headline: DiVincenzo de los Wolves autorizado para entrenar
caption: Donte DiVincenzo recibió el alta médica para participar en actividades de baloncesto tras su cirugía de tendón de Aquiles. Según el comunicado del Minnesota Timberwolves, el guardia avanza hacia su regreso y se espera que pueda debutar en la temporada alrededor de Año Nuevo. Mientras tanto, Anthony Edwards sigue fuera por una cirugía de rodilla y el equipo se mantiene competitivo con la incorporación de LaMelo Ball, ocupando el tercer puesto del Oeste con 13‑5.

title: Caitlin Clark: Playing Augusta on her 'bucket list' during WNBA offseason
description: During the WNBA offseason, Caitlin Clark said it's on her "bucket list" to play at Augusta for the first time.
article_context:
Caitlin Clark heads into the WNBA offseason with golf on her mind, specifically one course. She has never played the home of the Masters.
"I want to play Augusta for the first time," Clark said on the "New Heights" podcast with Jason and Travis Kelce. "I haven't played there yet. I have a couple of opportunities to do that, so I'm looking forward to that. That's probably on my bucket list."
She said she has a 15 handicap index and that she's hitting her drives in the 230-yard range, giving her a wedge into most greens when she's playing the forward tees.
Clark said she recently played The Grove XXIII in Florida owned by Michael Jordan, which she called "not very challenging." That was intended as a compliment.
"It's like a fun, good hang course, where you actually feel good about golfing," Clark said. "Some of these places are so challenging it's not even fun."
headline: Caitlin Clark quiere jugar Augusta en su offseason
caption: Durante la pausa de la WNBA, la estrella Caitlin Clark declaró que jugar en Augusta, la sede del Masters, está en su lista de deseos. Comentó su handicap de 15, sus drives de 230 yardas y que recientemente jugó en The Grove XXIII de Florida, describiéndolo como un campo "divertido y agradable".

title: Koepka's return ultimately improved PGA Tour status for Day, 2 others
description: Jason Day, Max McGreevy and Pontus Nyholm all moved up a spot in the final FedEx Cup standings because of Brooks Koepka's return, improving their tour status.
article_context:
ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. -- PGA Tour players were allowed to move up in the FedEx Cup standings and on the career money list in 2022 to account for the defections to LIV Golf. Now three players will be able to move up their status because of someone who came back.
That would be Brooks Koepka , who returned this year under a "Returning Member Program" once he was able to get out of his LIV contract. Among the stipulations for his return was two players added to the field each time he played.
David Skinns (38 points in one event), Séamus Power (28 points in two events) and A.J. Ewart (27 points in one event) took advantage, though not enough to affect their standing.
However, the PGA Tour did not want Koepka to affect another player's ranking for eligibility in 2027. The five-time major champion finished at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup.
That means Jason Day moves up one spot to No. 110, giving him conditional status in a category that will remain the same (no reshuffle) all year. Day also could choose a career money exemption.
Max McGreevy tied for 10th at the RSM Classic and narrowly missed out on the top 125 for conditional status. But with Koepka ahead of him, McGreevy now is No. 125. Pontus Nyholm goes from No. 151 -- no status at all -- to conditional status at No. 150.
headline: Koepka's regreso eleva estatus de Day, McGreevy y Nyholm
caption: Brooks Koepka volvió al PGA Tour bajo el programa de miembros retornantes, lo que permite que dos jugadores suban de posición cada vez que compite. Gracias a su regreso, Jason Day subió al puesto 110 del FedEx Cup y obtuvo estatus condicional; Max McGreevy alcanzó el puesto 125 y también quedó con estatus condicional; y Pontus Nyholm pasó del 151 al 150, asegurando también estatus condicional.

title: Senegal reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners over Morocco by CAS ruling
description: Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling.
article_context:
More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal are Africa's champions once again.
Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling that handed the trophy to Morocco .
Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations on the field in a chaotic final in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because their players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
- AFCON 2025 Final: Nothing could have been more embarrassing for African football
CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, citing referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.
"Once again and forever, champions of Africa," the Senegalese soccer federation posted on social media.
Tournament regulations said a team that refuses to play should be considered to have lost the game, but CAS said those rules were meant only for cases "when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently."
Ndala "did not err in law" when he resumed the game, CAS added.
"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," CAS said. "However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."
Morocco's soccer federation detailed plans for an appeal that targets one of the three judges on the CAS panel.
In a statement, the Moroccan federation protested what it described as the court's failure to address potential integrity concerns, alleging "confirmed communication" between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Fall, the Senegalese soccer president, 48 hours before the decision was issued.
The CAS director general, Matthieu Reeb, acknowledged to reporters at the court in Lausanne that a Moroccan protest was received just minutes before the verdict was announced.
Reeb said the court's panel "in charge of petitions for challenge has conceded that there was not enough elements at this stage to postpone the notification of the award."
CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court, also in Lausanne, though only on limited procedural grounds of which a judge's integrity could be one.
Haas has been among the most respected and in-demand CAS judges in the past 20 years, selected by parties in storied cases involving Manchester City beating a Champions League ban by UEFA, tennis star Simona Halep's doping case and Africa's Champions League final in 2019.
Patrick Kabou, a lawyer for the Senegalese Soccer Federation, called the alleged communication between Fall and Haas "unreal."
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) said that it "respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it."
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. Even the ball boys were involved in scuffles as they tried to snatch towels that Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy was using to keep his gloves dry.
The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by CAF.
Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. At 0-0, Senegal's team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.
Match referee Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco's penalty by Brahim Diaz was saved, and Senegal won in extra time.
The drama continued through the months of legal tussles. Senegal's players paraded with the trophy ahead of a game in March against Peru, even though Morocco was recognized as the champion at that point. Both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves to be the rightful champion of Africa.
Senegal had the laws of the game on its side, and Morocco had the tournament regulations.
The laws of soccer state that referee decisions are final. CAS backed that position with its own "field of play" doctrine, that on-field calls by a referee generally can't be taken to the sports court.
"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met -- both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume," CAS said.
In the first legal case in March, CAF appeal judges cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition."
The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month, and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.
The Senegalese federation (FSF) said it welcomed the ruling with "deep satisfaction."
"Far from consecrating the pre-eminence of one party over another, this decision affirms above all the triumph of sporting fairness and recalls a cardinal principle: the truth of a match is established exclusively on the field, under the protection of sports law," the federation said in its statement.
The next men's AFCON starts in June co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. Morocco will aim to end a wait for the title, which now stands at 50 years.
Th Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.
headline: CAS restituye a Senegal la Copa Africana de Naciones
caption: El Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (CAS) anuló la resolución de la CAF que daba a Marruecos un 3-0 por abandono y confirmó el 1-0 de Senegal en la final disputada en enero. El fallo se apoya en que el árbitro Jean-Jacques Ndala reanudó el partido y el penal de Brahim Diaz fue atajado; para el CAS, la norma de derrota por negarse a jugar solo aplica si el árbitro suspende el encuentro de forma definitiva. Marruecos anunció que recurrirá y cuestiona al árbitro del CAS Ulrich Haas por una supuesta comunicación con Fall, presidente de la federación senegalesa; el CAS sostuvo que no había elementos para postergar el fallo. ¿Debe un título decidirse meses después en los tribunales?

title: Son Heung-Min: Thomas Müller spot-on about lack of pressure in MLS
description: LAFC forward Son Heung-Min has backed Thomas Müller's comments about the "careless" playing style in the MLS and the lack of pressure that players feel due to the absence of a promotion/relegation system.
headline: Son Heung-Min respalda a Thomas Müller y la falta de presión
caption: El delantero de LAFC Son Heung-Min respalda las críticas de Thomas Müller sobre el estilo de juego y la falta de presión que percibe la plantilla por la ausencia de un sistema de ascenso y descenso. Para Son, el problema no es solo el fútbol: es el contexto. ¿Debería la MLS asumir más responsabilidad o los jugadores aceptar un ritmo sin castigo?

title: ⚽ 'Ted Lasso' to return for Season 5 on Apple TV
description: A release date for the upcoming season of the award-winning show has yet to be announced.
article_context:
"Ted Lasso" is coming back for a fifth season.
Apple TV announced the series' renewal in a news release Monday . The fourth season covered the eponymous Lasso -- a former American college football coach who made a dramatic career change by coaching a struggling Premier League team -- as he returned to AFC Richmond to coach its second-division women's team. The season ended with him stepping down to the assistant coach position to spend more time with his family.
Thanks for believing. #TedLasso has been renewed for Season 5. https://t.co/epfW8riG7b
"Ted Lasso" won back-to-back Emmy Awards for outstanding comedy series for its first two seasons. Jason Sudeikis, who plays Lasso, also won two outstanding lead actor in a comedy series awards for those seasons. The show also stars Hannah Waddingham, Brett Goldstein, Juno Temple and Jeremy Swift.
A release date for the upcoming season has not yet been announced.
headline: Ted Lasso tendrá quinta temporada en Apple TV
caption: La serie fue renovada para una quinta temporada, aunque todavía no hay fecha de estreno. La comedia ganó dos Emmy consecutivos como mejor serie de comedia y cerró su cuarta entrega con Lasso pasando a ser asistente para dedicar más tiempo a su familia. ¿Conseguirá la nueva temporada justificar la espera?

title: Transfer rumors, news: PSG eye Estêvão and Luis Díaz amid injury woes
description: Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão to their shortlist. Transfer Talk has the latest.
article_context:
Bayern Munich 's Luis Díaz and Chelsea 's Estêvão are on the shortlist of UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain , while Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett is being tracked by Chelsea. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.
Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades
- Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich 's Luis Díaz and Chelsea 's Estêvão to their shortlist, as they consider whether to strengthen their forward line following the long-term injuries sustained by Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , according to Diario AS . PSG manager Luis Enrique wants to take time before making a decision, amid plans to assess the squad in the coming weeks, but the club have identified the 29-year-old Díaz as an option due to his direct dribbling style and Estêvão, 19, is also on the Ligue 1 club's radar due to his limited minutes in London.
- Chelsea are keeping tabs on Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett , who is closing in on signing a new contract, the Daily Telegraph reports . The Blues are watching the 18-year-old's situation alongside Borussia Dortmund , but Spurs are reportedly now handling the final details on an extension which could ward off interest in his signature. Williams-Barnett registered a goal and an assist on his first Premier League start in the 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.
- Manchester United are preparing an approach for United States and Villarreal right back Alex Freeman , Football Insider reports . Scouts are reported to have been impressed by the 22-year-old's performances on multiple occasions, and the Red Devils have made him one of their top priorities for January in a move that would see him reunite with former USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino. title: Golliver's too-early NBA All-Star picks: The 24 most deserving players right now
description: So what if the All-Star Game is three months away? We're picking locks and position battles to watch across both conferences.
article_context:
There's a lot a basketball to be played before the 2027 NBA All-Star Game tips off in Phoenix on Feb. 21, but it's never too early to start surveying the field. With more than a month of regular-season games on the books, here's a rundown of the 12 most deserving candidates from each conference.
These picks were made to reward games played through Sunday and are not intended to be a projection of the rosters, which won't be announced until the new year. Criteria for selection included health, individual production, impact on winning and team success.
Note: Picks conform to the NBA's 2026 mandate of at least eight international players among the 24 selections. The NBA has not yet announced whether last year's " U.S. vs. the World " tournament format will return.
The "Greek Freak" is back on track in South Beach after a contentious final season with the Milwaukee Bucks . Antetokounmpo, who ranks in the top five leaguewide in scoring and rebounding, is guiding the No. 6 offense that has ironed out some of its wrinkles after a rough opening week.
While there was some cause for concern that a string of lower-body injuries might limit his effectiveness, the 31-year-old forward remains a forces going downhill to the rim. Antetokounmpo is tied for second in dunks and is shooting 72.2% in the basket area. While the two-time MVP has enjoyed perfect availability to start the season, his health deserves continued scrutiny; he has missed or barely played in three of the last four All-Star Games due to injuries.
Cunningham has picked up right where he left off during the Pistons' 60-win campaign in 2025-26, with one noticeable improvement. The 25-year-old guard is back as Detroit's offensive playmaker, ranking in the top 10 in scoring and assists. But after struggling with ball-control issues in last year's playoffs, he is averaging a career-low 3.1 turnovers per game. In one of the most impressive individual efforts of the young season, Cunningham posted 52 points, 11 assists and no turnovers in a Nov. 12 double-overtime win over the Washington Wizards .
Thanks to Cunningham's extraordinary offensive impact and an elite team defense, the Pistons have weathered the early-season absence of center Jalen Duren and the offseason departure of Tobias Harris to remain in the East's playoff picture.
The 26-year-old Maxey is the youngest and least accomplished of Philadelphia's four stars, but he would be the first pick if they were all placed into a fantasy draft. The two-time All-Star is the leading scorer and most reliable night-to-night producer for the 76ers, who sit atop the East standings after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown during the offseason.
The not-so-secret key to Philadelphia's early success is its 12-0 record in clutch games. Maxey ranks third leaguewide in plus-minus during clutch situations, and his late-game brilliance was pivotal in wins over the Indiana Pacers and the Cleveland Cavaliers .
Tatum hasn't quite fully returned to his pre-Achilles tear form, but he's still been awfully good. The six-time All-Star has reestablished himself as the No. 1 option for a potent Boston offense and joins Luka Doncic as the only players averaging at least 26 points, six rebounds and six assists per game.
Tatum's career-high free throw rate is an especially positive indicator for his recovery and a welcome development for the Celtics' outside-in offense, which lost Brown over the summer. After finishing last in free throw attempts in 2025-26, Boston is up to 26th to start this campaign. The Celtics are back in the East's top tier, but there's room to climb higher if Tatum's outside shooting efficiency returns to his career standard.
Towns has channeled his disappointment at not receiving a contract extension last offseason into exceptional all-around play. While some of his teammates have battled malaise at the start of what figures to be a grueling title defense, Towns ranks in the top five at his position by player efficiency rating (PER) and win shares.
The 31-year-old center has helped compensate for Mitchell Robinson 's offseason departure with a career-high 13.9 rebounds per game, and he leads the NBA with 16 double-doubles. As the Knicks search for more reliable contributions from Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges , Towns has easily boasted the best net rating among New York's starters.
The 2026 Finals MVP accepted responsibility for the Knicks' 0-3 start -- "Everything falls on my shoulders," he said -- and he has been instrumental in stabilizing the team in recent weeks. New York's offensive efficiency has fallen well short of the level of its 2025-26 championship campaign, but Brunson has lifted it back into the top 10 over the past 10 games.
Brunson, 30, continues to rank among the league's top 10 scorers and is second in time of possession. So far, he is holding up well despite that high-usage role and his struggling teammates: The three-time All-Star hasn't missed a game and has upped his scoring and 3-point efficiency from last season.
The Cavaliers' stars all share blame for the team's thoroughly mediocre start after their conference finals appearance last season. James Harden was playing sluggish and sloppy basketball until he broke out with a 51-point effort against the Pacers on Friday, and Evan Mobley might never escape his cutting "18 and 8" nickname on social media.
Mitchell remains the leading scorer on a top-five Cleveland offense, though his production has slipped slightly as compared with that of last season. While there is a bigger conversation brewing about how Cleveland might pivot if it takes a step back in the playoffs, Mitchell's 24/4/5 averages look good enough to land his eighth straight All-Star selection.
When judging Brown's acclimation to Philadelphia after a blockbuster summer trade, one must differentiate between his strange off-court comments and his solid on-court play. Brown's passive-aggressive statements about Tatum blew up in his face when he played poorly in his first head-to-head matchup against his former teammate.
That sequence of events hasn't been representative of Brown's start in Philadelphia. He has slotted in nicely as a sturdy second option for the 76ers, who have kept winning despite poor shooting from Joel Embiid and inconsistent impact from James. Brown occupied a range of offensive roles during his 10 years in Boston, and that flexibility has been an asset since his big move.

title: La joven futbolista de River que recibió un regalo de Thiago Almada
description: Milagros Acevedo ya fue reconocida en el Monumental y, tres años después, se quedó con el short del Guayo tras la victoria ante Lanús.
article_context:
Milagros Acevedo recibió un regalo de Thiago Almada.
Con un aporte clave ya en su historial y un nuevo momento viralizado apenas tres años después, Milagros Acevedo volvió a quedar bajo los reflectores en una noche especial para River . Esta vez no fue por una intervención dentro del juego, como aquella ocasion en la que ayudó a acelerar una acción de ataque que finalizó en gol ante Colón en 2023, sino por un gesto de Thiago Almada luego del 3-1 frente a Lanús que clasificó al equipo de Leonardo Ponzio a los cuartos de final del Clausura .
La figura de la noche, autor de un doblete en el Monumental , se tomó algunos minutos después de atender a la prensa para saludar a quienes permanecían al costado del campo. En ese recorrido rumbo al túnel, Almada frenó ante el llamado de Acevedo y le entregó el short que había utilizado durante el encuentro . Una escena sencilla, pero que rápidamente se expandió en las redes por la repercusión que suele generar cada gesto de ese estilo por parte de los futbolistas.
Milagros no es una alcanzapelotas más dentro del club de Núñez. Además de cumplir esa función en distintos partidos del equipo masculino, forma parte de la Reserva del fútbol femenino del club y cuenta con un paso por la Selección Argentina Sub 17. Su nombre ya había trascendido en 2023, cuando protagonizó una acción que los hinchas todavía recuerdan.
Aquel día, en un Monumental repleto, el elenco de Martín Demichelis (acariciando el título de la Liga Profesional), recibía a Colón. En el segundo tiempo, Acevedo reaccionó con rapidez desde su posición como alcanzapelotas y le alcanzó una pelota a Milton Casco para reanudar el juego de inmediato. La jugada tomó mal parada a la defensa rival y terminó derivando en el gol de Lucas Beltrán . El episodio se hizo viral y hasta recibió elogios por la viveza con la que interpretó la acción.
La imagen recorrió las redes en cuestión de minutos y volvió a poner en escena a una chica que ya había sabido ganarse un lugar en el mundo River. Esta vez no hizo falta una avivada para acelerar una jugada de ataque ni una intervención decisiva en pleno partido. Alcanzó con un breve cruce al borde de la cancha para que una nueva historia vinculada a Milagros Acevedo volviera a captar la atención de los hinchas .

headline: Milagros Acevedo recibe short de Thiago Almada
caption: Milagros Acevedo, joven alcanzapelotas de la reserva femenina de River, recibió el short que utilizó Thiago Almada tras la victoria 3‑1 ante Lanús que clasificó al equipo de Leonardo Ponzio a los cuartos de final del Clausura. El gesto, que se viralizó en redes, recuerda su anterior protagonismo en 2023, cuando recuperó una pelota para Milton Casco y desencadenó el gol de Lucas Beltrán contra Colón.

title: Qué dijeron en Marruecos tras el fallo que le dio la Copa Africana de Naciones a Senegal: "Peligroso precedente"
description: La prensa marroquí reaccionó con distintas miradas a la resolución del TAS, que les sacó el título, y se los devolvió a los senegaleses.
article_context:
Walid Regragui y Hakimi en la final ante Senegal. (EFE/EPA/JALAL MORCHIDI)
A más de diez meses de la final, la Copa Africana de Naciones tiene un desenlace oficial. El Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) falló a favor de Senegal y le devolvió el título que había conseguido el 18 de enero, cuando derrotó 1-0 a Marruecos . La resolución dejó sin efecto la decisión de la Confederación Africana de Fútbol , que había retirado el título a los Leones de Teranga y declarado campeón a los marroquíes.
Y lógicamente, el fallo generó repercusiones en Marruecos , donde los principales medios analizaron las consecuencias deportivas e institucionales de la resolución. Con focos cuestionando a los procedimientos hasta intentos de dejar atrás la polémica, enfocándose en el crecimiento de la selección .
El portal marroquí fue uno de los más críticos con la resolución y tituló: " La decisión del TAS abre peligroso precedente para el fútbol mundial y trasciende el conflicto entre Marruecos y Senegal ". En su cuerpo agregó: "Lo que está en juego es la coherencia del derecho deportivo, la autoridad de los reglamentos y la credibilidad de las instituciones encargadas de garantizar la justicia en el fútbol internacional".
Además, planteó una pregunta sobre las posibles consecuencias futuras: " ¿Qué impedirá mañana que otros equipos reproduzcan este comportamiento en un Mundial o en la Champions League para presionar al árbitro y después regresar al terreno de juego? ".
Con una postura diferente, este medio eligió poner el acento en el futuro de la selección marroquí. " Para los Leones del Atlas, la historia continúa y sus ambiciones permanecen intactas ", fue el título de la nota. En el cuerpo, sostuvieron que el episodio no debería condicionar los objetivos del equipo.
"El asunto ya es cosa del pasado para los Leones del Atlas, cuyas ambiciones van mucho más allá de la decisión tomada en Lausana", publicaron. También agregaron: " Marruecos ha progresado lo suficiente como para que su trayectoria ya no pueda medirse con una sola final ".
"El TAS otorga el título a Senegal sobre Marruecos, absolviendo al árbitro final”, tituló el diario. Describió la resolución como el cierre de un conflicto que se extendió durante meses, sumó: "El veredicto ya está dado, sellando definitivamente una de las sagas más turbulentas de la historia reciente del fútbol continental ".
Sin embargo, también reconoció el impacto que tuvo la decisión en el país. " Para el fútbol marroquí, este fallo deja un sabor amargo ", ya que esperaban que se mantenga la decisión disciplinaria de la CAF.
El periódico eligió un título todavía más confrontativo: " ¿Puede Marruecos todavía frustrar el robo? ". En su artículo, consideró que el fallo representa un revés judicial para el país, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de que la disputa continúe.
Además, cuestionaron una supuesta llamada telefónica entre Abdoulaye Fall, presidente de la Federación Senegalesa, y Ulrich Haas, uno de los tres árbitros que analizaron el recurso de Senegal . "Si este intercambio se confirmara, plantearía serios interrogantes sobre el respeto a las normas procesales, en particular aquellas que rigen la independencia y la imparcialidad de los árbitros ", señalaron.
