title: Liga MX playoff preview: Will Cruz Azul win back-to-back titles?
description: The Liga MX playoffs are back to close out 2026! Who are some of the favorites and who can cause a surprise in the Liguilla?
article_context:
Welcome to the start of the Liga MX playoffs!
Following 17 matchdays, Liga MX's 2026 Apertura season will now enter the playoff stage with the final eight battling it out in the quarterfinal.
Glancing across those invited to the postseason, a handful of the usual giants are in the running. Prominent clubs such as Cruz Azul , Club América , Chivas , and Toluca are still in the race for this season's trophy.
Elsewhere, underdogs such as Atlas and Pachuca are set to shake things up.
With all that in mind, who are the favorites and who will look to disrupt the Mexican soccer scene? Split up into three tiers, let's dive into our team-by-team preview for the Liga MX playoffs.
It's been fairly smooth sailing for the current title holders, who have earned more victories than any other Liga MX team this season. What has been especially impressive for Cruz Azul is their recent form at home, where they've claimed a 4W-1D-0L record since September.
Only América have a greater roster market value ( according to Transfermarkt ) than Cruz Azul, and when glancing through their squad, there's a noteworthy depth of talent that head coach Joel Huiqui can bring off the bench. The likes of genuine Liga MX stars on other teams such as Andres Montaño , Osinachi Ebere , Nicolás Ibáñez , Angel Márquez and Luka Romero were substitutes in their last game against Chivas .
Despite this crop of players, Cruz Azul's backline has shown some occasional and surprising mistakes for the caliber of team that they are. Los Cementeros are second in the league when it comes to errors leading to shots and joint-league-leaders in errors leading to goals.
Nearly signed with AS Monaco over the summer and now likely playing his last Liga MX season before heading abroad, it's midfielder Érik Lira . The Mexico international is exceptionally well rounded in his role as the leader in the heart of the starting lineup and should be more than motivated to step up before an anticipated move to Europe in the winter.
Cruz Azul will fall just short in the final. Back-to-back titles are an immense challenge for the Mexico City-based side, and despite how strong they've been at their home ground and the ability for Huiqui to easily shift through different formations, it's tough to trust the side that has taken a couple of steps back defensively.
That means some additional work from either Kevin Mier or Andrés Gudiño in net, and both have been fairly lackluster when it comes to their goals-prevented tallies in the Apertura.
Regular-season record: 9W-6D-2L (1st place) Number of league titles: 12
A shaky start that then developed into a very promising route to the playoffs. Chivas have only lost one Liga MX match since July 25 and have collected four wins from their past five. Not bad for manager Gabriel Milito & Co.
Their high possession dictates the pace of most games, which is also an "offense is the best defense" approach for the squad that has only allowed 15 goals across 17 matches. In their last five matches to close out the regular season, Los Rojiblancos earned three shutouts.
But how efficient and dangerous are they in the final third? Despite having more of the ball than all but one team, Chivas are seventh when it comes to goals scored and 11th league-wide for xG.
Herculez Gomez and Alejandro Moreno debate the biggest storylines and break down the best highlights that soccer in the Americas has to offer. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only)
With a squad that only utilizes Mexican players, Chivas have a tendency to uplift the next generation of domestic stars, one of which is 19-year-old Santiago Sandoval . The forward/attacking midfielder has earned four goal contributions in his past six games for club and country, and has begun making an impact for the Mexico national team after his debut earlier this year.
Things are clicking for Chivas under Milito. Pachuca are a genuine dark horse that will make things tricky in the quarterfinal, but the Guadalajara side should squeeze past them and eventually lift the title for the first time since 2017. Milito's tactical approach and home-field advantage as the No. 1 seed will clinch the trophy.
Regular-season record: 7W-4D-6L (8th place) Number of league titles: 7
It all looked a bit erratic until, well, an eye-catching finish with 11 goals scored across four victories to close out the season. Although they sneaked into the quarterfinal with a spot at eighth place, Los Tuzos defeated three separate playoff teams during that four-game winning streak.
Tigres , the lone non-playoff team that they defeated, was also a giant in Mexican soccer not too long ago. No team has more momentum than Pachuca.
Take a bow, Carlos Moreno . The goalkeeper leads the league in goals prevented (+3.91) and was consistent in net throughout the Apertura. Yet to make his senior national team debut, it's a genuine surprise that Mexico coach Rafael Márquez has yet to give him a chance.
As for their Achilles' heel? That's an over-reliance on striker Salomón Rondón . Credit is due to the forward who led the league with 17 goals this season, but time and time again we've seen that when he has an off day, so does his club. Shut down their striker, and most of the defensive work is done for the opponent.
We're repeating ourselves here, but what makes or breaks Pachuca's playoff run is Rondón. He's got 20 goal contributions in 17 games; he's the obvious focal point in the attack, and he's charging into the postseason with four goals and three assists during Pachuca's four-game winning streak.
Although we've placed them atop the underdog rankings, they'll lose to Chivas. It'll be more competitive than expected, especially for a team that's only here due to goal differential, but the No. 1 seed will narrowly brush past them. Keep an eye, either way, on Rondón.
Regular-season record: 8W-6D-3L (3rd place) Number of league titles: 16
Just when it looked like América had a path to cement their spot at the top of the standings, the Liga MX giants then stumbled through a 0W-3D-2L record to close out the season.
Heading into the playoffs, the atmosphere is clearly a tense one, with head coach Guillermo Almada having to reassert that he has "confidence in the players" after losing 1-0 to Tigres in the final regular season weekend.
Almada's attack is a potent one. Even though the team hasn't won a game since October, Club América still closed things out with a league-best 38 goals and a +14 goal differential. If anything, we might be und

title: Man United will need big January transfer spending to avoid relegation
description: Manchester United have a choice: Spend £150 million on new players in January or lose £300 million if they get relegated at the end of the Premier League season.
article_context:
Manchester United are on the edge of a huge financial dilemma: Spend £150 million on new players in January, or risk relegation from the Premier League and the prospect of losing more than twice that figure by being outside the richest league in the world.
United's owners, the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group, must roll the dice in the transfer market and hope they get lucky, because one of the world's biggest and most celebrated clubs really could be playing against Wrexham, Millwall and Lincoln in the EFL Championship next season.
Former United captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville both asserted, in the immediate aftermath of Sunday's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield, that the 20-time English champions will not be relegated this season, but the Premier League table suggests United are sleepwalking into the absolute humiliation of relegation.
United are second bottom, with eight points from 11 games -- that's 10 fewer points than Tottenham had at this stage last season and they survived only on the final day of the campaign with a two-point cushion between themselves and relegated West Ham, who had 10 points from 11 games.
When United were last relegated from the top-flight in 1973-74, the team won three of its first 11 league games. This season, United have won just once, against promoted Ipswich Town in August.
And to put sharp focus on the alarming problems new coach Mauricio Pochettino must address, United now have the worst defensive record of any team in Europe's Big Five leagues after seeing their goals against tally reach 34 at Anfield -- one more than Crystal Palace , the Premier League's bottom club.
Watch your favorite events in the newly enhanced ESPN App. Learn more about what plan is right for you. Sign Up Now
So while Neville and Keane are not yet ready to think the unthinkable, the United hierarchy can't afford to display the same complacency. Sunday's performance against Liverpool, after so many other defeats this season, proved that the squad inherited by Pochettino desperately needs reinforcements to drag the team clear of danger.
United spent just over £150 million to bring in three midfielders ( Carlos Baleba , Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans ) in the summer but neglected to bolster an aging and injury-prone defense.
The club's recruitment team, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, also opted against signing attacking additions, with United taking the view that Marcus Rashford 's return from successive loans at Aston Villa and Barcelona would increase the options available to Pochettino's predecessor Michael Carrick.
Sources have told ESPN that Carrick quietly pushed for more signings, but with Wilcox operating within a tight budget laid down by Ratcliffe and CEO Omar Berrada, the money was simply not there for further signings.
Despite Berrada's delusional comments last week that United's summer recruitment had "made the squad fundamentally better," the league table tells another story and the long-term injury absences of winger Rashford, left back Luke Shaw and center forward Benjamin Sesko this season have exposed the negligence -- and false economy -- of the club's spending. But the January window offers United a chance to rebuild midseason, even if their recent track record suggests they probably won't.
Despite United's most recent financial accounts highlighting disturbing levels of debt -- the club owe £1.1 billion in loans and outstanding transfer fees -- and a pre-tax loss of £43 million, the Premier League's new squad cost ratio (SCR) rules offer them headroom to spend their way out of trouble in January.
Clubs can now spend up to 85% of football-related revenue, and United posted record revenues of £677.6 million last season. So while finances are tight, United have the ability to sign new players, especially with £160 million still available in their rotating credit facility.
Download the ESPN app and enable Mark Ogden's news alerts to receive push notifications for the latest updates first. Opt in by tapping the alerts bell in the top right corner. For more information, click here .
If Pochettino is backed in January, with Newcastle and England left back Lewis Hall (even though he signed a new contract over the summer), an obvious target to replace Shaw, the right additions could be transformative.
It is clear that United need to improve in all areas; they need experience, athleticism and a greater goal threat, and those qualities don't come cheap.
But the alternative to spending in January would be to take a massive gamble on Pochettino's ability to coax the existing squad away from danger and keep finances in place for more strategic signings in the summer.
United simply can't afford to take that gamble; the potential downside is far greater than the cost of spending big in January.
The club banked £191.5 million in Premier League prize money last season, but the EFL TV deal is worth just £5.7 million a year to clubs in the Championship.
If the worst-case scenario were to happen then United would receive a relegation parachute payment of approximately £45 million in their first year outside the Premier League, but an instant drop of £150 million in earnings would only be the start before loss of commercial revenue and the cost of servicing huge player contracts, or letting stars leave for knockdown prices, comes into play.
So while spending even more money in January and adding to the club's debt mountain will give United's accountants sleepless nights, the alternative is much worse. The consequences of relegation are enormous.

caption: El equipo necesita invertir £150 millones en nuevos jugadores en enero para evitar el descenso, ya que la relegación podría costarles £300 millones. Actualmente, el equipo está segundo desde abajo en la tabla de la Premier League con solo 8 puntos en 11 partidos.

title: In limbo, Smith, 33, prepared to pave 'difficult' path back to PGA Tour
description: Having moved past LIV Golf, Australian Cameron Smith, 33, is preparing to pave his path back to the PGA Tour, but he knows "there's plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it's going to be difficult."
headline: Cameron Smith busca regresar
caption: El golfista australiano de 33 años se prepara para regresar al PGA Tour después de su paso por LIV Golf, pero reconoce que será un camino difícil debido a la competencia de otros jugadores.

title: Penge birdies No. 18 twice to win RSM playoff and keep PGA Tour card
description: Marco Penge went from the verge of losing his PGA Tour card to winning the season finale at the RSM Classic on Monday in a four-way playoff.
article_context:
ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. -- Marco Penge went from the verge of losing his PGA Tour card to winning the season finale at the RSM Classic on Monday, making birdie on the 18th hole to be part of a four-way playoff and winning on the first extra hole with a 4-foot birdie putt.
Penge, who closed with a 5-under 65, was the only player to birdie the par-4 18th on the Seaside course all four times he played it, and it proved valuable in so many ways.
The 28-year-old from England, who was No. 120 in the FedEx Cup coming into Sea Island, now has a two-year exemption that puts him in the Championship Series with its $20 million prize funds when it starts in 2028.
Michael Thorbjornsen , already a PGA Tour winner this year at the Rocket Classic, missed a 6-foot birdie putt in regulation for the win. He shot 67. Haotong Li of China closed with a 65 and Max Greyserman shot 66 to be part of the playoff. All three missed birdie chances after Penge stuffed wedge into 4 feet.
"The last four, five weeks has been really tough with my game," Penge said. "I've just been putting the work in and I said to my team as long as I give everything I can, the result is the result. If I lose my card and stuff like that, then it is what it is. I'm over the moon."
The result was particularly crushing for Li, who was at No. 134 in the FedEx Cup.
He was projected to get his card until Thorbjornsen in the final group made birdie on the 18th to make it a four-way playoff, and then Penge wound up winning. The three-way tie for third moved Li to No. 103, just over 10 points shy of the top 100 for a full card in 2027.
He thought he had his card when he headed to the playoff, and learned only after it was over that it wasn't enough.
"But everything's done for a reason," Li said. "I could have to go somewhere next year and play at DP (World Tour in Europe), so there's so many consequence in life, so you've just got to keep up and doing what you're doing. The result will come."
By the end of a cool, overcast and quiet Monday finish in the rain-delayed tournament, Penge was the only player to move into the top 100, bumping out David Lipsky , who missed the cut.
It's not all bad for the likes of Li and Rasmus Hojgaard of Denmark, who was in position to move into the top 100 until he played the final five holes with a bogey and four pars. Those who finish from Nos. 101 through 110 have conditional status that goes unchanged for the year.
Davis Thompson , who lives at Sea Island and whose father is the tournament director, has a recent history of being on the wrong side of the bubble and this looked to be another such occasion. He was 4 over through seven holes, rallied to get back in position and then finished bogey-bogey that left him clinging to the 100th spot.
"Just got off to a terrible start, which sucks. And then obviously the finish sucked even worse," Thompson said when he left, fearing for the worst. "I just didn't execute down the stretch, which is kind of the theme of the year. Just got to move on."
Greyserman now has six runner-up finishes without a PGA Tour victory, and this looked to be his week when he made birdie on the 13th to open a two-shot lead. But he took four shots from 38 yards on the par-5 15th to make bogey and closed with three straight pars.
He had an 18-foot birdie chance in regulation for the win.
It was a beautiful end of the PGA Tour season for Penge, who earned his card as the leading player in Europe last year not already eligible. But he took six weeks off after dealing with a sinus problem and vertigo, wanting to return at full health.
"I always seem to play my best golf when my back's up against the wall," Penge said. "I've been through this before on the DP World Tour, keeping my card in the last event and dealing with adversity and coming back from health issues, all that stuff. So I knew I could do it.
"I just wasn't sure I ever had the game this week to be able to do it," he said. "And thankfully I did."
It was the second straight Monday finish on the PGA Tour because of heavy rain that forced the third round to be played on Sunday.
headline: Penge gana RSM Classic
caption: Marco Penge ganó el RSM Classic en un playoff de cuatro jugadores, asegurando su tarjeta para el PGA Tour. Penge birdieó el hoyo 18 dos veces para obtener la victoria.

title: 'My mouth was open in horror': Patten drops Heliovaara to team up with Skupski
description: Henry Patten has ended his world No. 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion and agreed to team up with British compatriot Neal Skupski.
article_context:
Henry Patten has ended his world No. 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion and agreed to team up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.
Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.
However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the exuberant Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to reveal their partnership after three grand-slam titles was over -- despite a previous agreement they would continue.
"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn. Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year," Heliovaara said on his own blog website.
"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.
"He didn't want to play together again next year, even though we had agreed to do so during the fall. The announcement came as completely as it could come and I couldn't help but listen with my mouth open in horror and say that I don't agree at all.
"I'm unlikely to ever fully understand what and why this ultimately happened.
"The emotional scale in my head was quite violent at first, a shocking situation in any case.
"The two-and-a-half years with Henry have been by far the best time of my career, for which I am eternally grateful to him, but now the main feeling was heavy disappointment and even anger."
- Consistent Zverev earns final No. 1 ATP ranking despite loss to Alcaraz - Carlos Alcaraz defeats top-ranked Alexander Zverev in ATP Finals
Heliovaara confirmed in his blog that he would team up with Britain's Julian Cash , while Patten is set to partner Skupski in 2027.
headline: Patten abandona a Heliovaara
caption: Henry Patten terminó su sociedad con Harri Heliovaara y se unirá a Neal Skupski en 2027, según acuerdo reciente. La pareja había ganado tres títulos de Grand Slam juntos.

title: Cleveland Cavaliers become first NBA team to practice at Obama Presidential Center
description: The WNBA was the first professional sports league to use the court, playing there at All-Star Weekend in July.
article_context:
CHICAGO -- The Cleveland Cavaliers hosted a shootaround at the Obama Presidential Center on Monday morning, becoming the first NBA team to practice at the facility that opened in Chicago over the summer.
The WNBA became the first professional sports league to use the court during All-Star Weekend in July, and its players were given a surprise visit from former President Barack Obama . And although he was not in town Monday morning, Cavs guard Donovan Mitchell still called it an "honor and a blessing" to use the courts.
"As a Black male, you have to come and see this, seeing the first Black president build something like this in his hometown in the city of Chicago, what this represents, what this means," Mitchell said. "I have to come back and at least appreciate every detail put into this place for sure."
The Cavs are in Chicago to play the Chicago Bulls on Monday night at the United Center, so Cleveland's players did not have time to take a tour of the library during this visit, though some of their front office members and other staff went for a tour after the shootaround.
The Cavaliers became the first team EVER to practice on Home Court at the Obama Presidential Center, taking the floor ahead of tonight's matchup with the Bulls. #LetEmKnow https://t.co/6YiPeSRclD
Mitchell said he plans to return in the future. He said he met Obama at a golf outing a few years ago, and although the Cavs star joked that he played "the worst round of golf" in his life, the two have maintained ties.
"I would've never thought that I'd have a relationship with him," Mitchell said. "For him to know me, to know my game, numbers. To know my wife's songs," he said of singer-songwriter Coco Jones, "to talk about how him and the first lady listened to her songs.
"It just shows you how much an orange basketball can bring so many people together from different places, different cultures, different areas. And having it in a place like this is really a big symbol of -- just because you're president of the United States, you can still hoop and get some buckets. Having known President Obama and having been around him, this is him. This is exactly who he is."
Cavs center Jarrett Allen said the facility had everything ready for an NBA team, and he called the experience extraordinary. The Cavs took a team trip to Spain for training camp over the summer, and he noted how those bonding experiences would help build chemistry going forward.
Allen took note of the decal around the court, including one of Obama's most iconic phrases, "Yes, we can," being painted across the baseline.
It echoed a message from Cavs president Koby Altman, who addressed the team before the start of shoot around to note the significance of the court the players stood on.
"Obama being the first Black president was something that some people never thought would happen," Allen said. "When you see something that tough to overcome ... we're facing adversity every single day. There's stuff that we think we can't overcome. But looking at somebody like him overcome a barrier like that, we can do anything."
headline: Cavaliers practican en Obama Presidential Center
caption: El equipo de la NBA se convirtió en el primero en practicar en el centro, que ya había sido utilizado por la WNBA durante el All-Star Weekend en julio. El base Donovan Mitchell calificó la experiencia de "honor y bendición"

title: The best tennis players of 2026: Zverev, Rybakina and many more
description: As the 2026 tennis season comes to a close, we name the top players and moments of the year.
article_context:
The 2026 professional tennis season has come to an end, and what a wild, unpredictable, slightly chaotic year it was.
From the long-awaited emergence of Elena Rybakina to the surprising rise of Alexander Zverev to the countless stunning upsets and heralded comebacks and farewells, 2026 truly was one to remember.
Few could have predicted at the start of the year how the majors would fare. Rybakina won two, as did Zverev. Aryna Sabalenka didn't earn a Slam trophy for the first time since 2022. Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner , who had combined to win every major in 2024 and 2025, struggled with injuries and each added only one more to their growing collections. Mirra Andreeva and Linda Noskova claimed their first Slam titles, at the French Open and Wimbledon, respectively.
Yup, it all made for one unforgettable -- and, did we mention, unpredictable -- year.
Who deserves to take home the top honors for 2026? Here are our WTA and ATP Players of the Year, in addition to some more titles on other (perhaps slightly less-quantifiable) favorites from the year.
After she won her first major title at Wimbledon in 2022, few could dispute Rybakina's talent and potential, but injuries, illnesses and some off-the-court setbacks dictated much of her next few seasons.
After winning the WTA Finals to close out 2025, a resurgent Rybakina was virtually unstoppable at the Australian Open. With her dominant -- and often spirit-crushing -- serve and cool-as-ice demeanor, Rybakina didn't allow top-level opponents such as Iga Swiatek and Jessica Pegula to win a set. In the final, in a rematch of the 2023 tournament final, Rybakina secured her revenge against Sabalenka with a 6-4, 4-6, 6-4 victory.
"She played [an] incredible match," Sabalenka said afterward.
Rybakina reached the final at Indian Wells and won her second title at Stuttgart in April on the clay, but it was the summer hard-court season where she officially proved her championship mentality and made her case for the world No. 1 ranking. The 27-year-old advanced to the final at the Canadian Open, but after retiring because of an Achilles injury during a quarterfinal match at the Cincinnati Open, her status for the US Open was in doubt. She was unable to practice for a week -- a near eternity in the lead-up to a Slam -- before the major got underway.
No one, Rybakina included, knew what to expect from her when the tournament began. But she quickly quieted any speculation with one strong showing after another throughout the tournament. Defeating Coco Gauff in three sets in the semifinals -- and all but silencing the American crowd at Arthur Ashe Stadium in the decider -- Rybakina defeated Sabalenka yet again in the final for her third major title and second of the year.
"I always believed that it [was] possible," Rybakina told reporters after the final. "We've been having great results. Of course, not every year is the same. I won Wimbledon in 2022. Then I wasn't winning the Slams, but I played the final of Australian Open the next year. I think we were always there.
"It's never easy. Even now I finish here, I rest, I celebrate, and then still the tournaments are coming up. You still need to play. You still need to compete with the same players, and you still need to do your best. It's an amazing journey, and hopefully I can continue [to] stay at the top as long as possible."
Two days later, she took over the world No.1 ranking from Sabalenka, who'd held it for 99 weeks.
Rybakina collected another trophy at the 500-level Ningbo Open before having to withdraw and shut down her season at the WTA Finals due to illness. She now has a slim lead over Andreeva atop the rankings -- but was the clear choice for Player of the Year and she should remain a contender for every Slam in 2027.
Entering the year with an 0-3 streak in major finals and a lopsided losing record against both Alcaraz and Sinner, Zverev was an unlikely candidate to win two major titles and claim the world No. 1 ranking.
But no one capitalized on the extended absences and upsets of the Big Two more than the 29-year-old German. While top seed after top seed -- including Sinner -- faltered at Roland Garros, Zverev stayed the course. In the final, he defeated Flavio Cobolli in five sets, 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 to finally secure what he had been working toward for his entire career.
"We've been through injuries," an emotional Zverev said to his team during the trophy presentation. "We've been through heartbreak. We've been through losses. We've been losers at times in the important moments. But at the end of the day, we're Grand Slam champions now and that's what counts."
Just weeks later, he reached his first Wimbledon final, where he lost to Sinner. And at the US Open, he once again seized the opportunity with Sinner's absence and after Alcaraz's quarterfinal loss in his first event back.
Zverev had to fight through tricky early opponents -- needing five sets in both of his first two matches -- but he then was in firm control of his destiny. He didn't drop another set until the final against Ben Shelton , but even that was just a temporary hiccup. He won his second Slam title 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2.
When Sinner announced he would not be able to return for the rest of the year, Zverev's path was cleared. He would be the year-end No. 1, marking his first time achieving the milestone ranking. He closed out the year with a loss to Alcaraz in the title match at the ATP Finals on Sunday.
A polarizing figure in the sport due to multiple domestic violence allegations , Zverev has also faced many questions about the legitimacy of his top ranking due to a poor top-10 record and lopsided head-to-head showings against Sinner and Alcaraz -- punctuated by his loss to Alcaraz on Sunday. Zverev's stay at the top might ultimately be one of the more forgettable stints in recent memory. (Although he jokingly told reporters his five losses to Sinner in 2026 shouldn't count because "he's a robot.")
Still, it would be impossible to discount what he has accomplished on the court this season, and he is undisputedly the player of the year for what he has been able to do.
Since bursting onto the scene as a 15-year-old in 2023, Andreeva's future as a major champion seemed all but inevitable. But still, having the potential and fulfilling it are two different things.

headline: Rybakina y Zverev, jugadores del año
caption: Elena Rybakina y Alexander Zverev han sido nombrados jugadores del año en la WTA y la ATP, respectivamente, después de una temporada llena de giros inesperados y momentos destacados en el tenis profesional.

title: Lazio are top of Serie A despite their fans boycotting the team's owner
description: Lazio's success this season has been one of the big stories in Serie A, made more remarkable by the fact that their fans won't attend home games until the club is sold.
article_context:
We're approaching the end of November and Lazio are top of Serie A , with 32 points in 12 games. The last time it happened was more than 25 years ago and back then, soccer -- and Lazio -- were entirely different animals.
The Lazio team that would win the league in 1999-2000 was an expensively assembled super club -- so expensively assembled, in fact, that they'd go bankrupt a few seasons later. They boasted Siniša Mihajlović and Alessandro Nesta at the back, Juan Sebastián Verón, Diego Simeone and future Ballon d'Or winner Pavel Nedvěd in midfield, Marcelo Salas, Alen Bokšić and Simone Inzaghi up front. Coaching them was the late Sven-Göran Eriksson, who a year later would leverage the gig into the England job, becoming the Three Lions' first foreign manager.
The Lazio team doing it in 2026-27 are built on a shoestring, a function of an unpopular owner perennially accused of underinvestment. Still, they're a colorful -- if unremarkable -- bunch.
Their standout goalkeeper, Christos Mandas , is in his first full season at a starter, having played just 90 minutes of cup football last year. Right back Romano Floriani has a famous great-grandfather (Benito Mussolini), and an even more famous great-aunt (Sophia Loren). Their big summer signing, former Inter Milan super-sub Davide Frattesi (he made just 18 league starts in three seasons), has an influencer sister who dated Weston McKennie . Their playmaker, Reda Belahyane , started just six games in 18 months at the club before this year and was widely considered a bust until now. Their center back, Oliver Provstgaard , did win the Champions League in 2021 ... albeit the esports Champions League.
And then there's the manager, Gennaro Gattuso, last seen in charge of Italy 's national team in April where he lost a do-or-die playoff to Bosnia-Herzegovina and denied the Azzurri a shot at the World Cup , a tournament nobody -- other than Brazil -- has won more times. Lazio is Gattuso's 11th job. None of his previous ones lasted more than two seasons, and his average tenure has been 41 weeks.
All this -- and Lazio's recent history of unremarkably finishing seventh, seventh and ninth -- would make their top spot an underdog story. But the remarkable part is that they're doing it with almost no home support after a fan boycott that began last January.
Lazio's average attendance through their first five home games has been around 10,000 spectators per game, a bleak number in the 70,000-seat cavern that is Rome's Stadio Olimpico. When you then consider that even that number is inflated by visiting supporters who often outnumber Lazio fans -- as happened for the visit of AC Milan in September, when the crowd was 21,000-strong -- you get a sense of how surreal the notion of "home support" is for these players.
For context, Lazio averaged around 44,000 a game in the two full seasons before the boycott, but season-ticket sales cratered from 29,918 in 2025-26 to less than 3,000 this year.
The boycott began as the culmination of a long-running dispute between Claudio Lotito (who has owned the club since 2004) and the club's hardcore supporters known as ultras , though fans of all stripes quickly joined in. Their main gripe is a perceived lack of respect toward the fanbase, a lack of ambition and a general sense of drift at the club. They demand that Lotito put Lazio up for sale, something he is refusing to do.
Lazio supporters say it's painful not being there to cheer on their side at home games, but describe it as "an act of love," and they try to make up for it in other ways. Ahead of each match at the Stadio Olimpico, they gather outside to greet the team bus and the players with flares, songs and banners, pep-rally style, before going off to watch the game, often communally. Away matches are all sold out, and often they've managed to secure additional tickets from the opposing club.
Caught in the middle between the fans and the club are the players and Gattuso. In keeping with his straight-talking image, Gattuso isn't mincing words, while also threading the needle (a balancing act he manages better than most).
"We miss the fans, playing in a stadium that's 20% full sucks: it's like COVID all over again," he said. "For me, football without fans isn't football, it's another sport, you might as well go and take your dog for a walk.
"The fans are suffering too; it's killing them inside not coming to see us. But I have to respect their decision, because they're showing integrity. And I thank them for the tremendous support they are showing us in other ways."
Watch your favorite events in the newly enhanced ESPN App. Learn more about what plan is right for you. Sign Up Now
For his part, Lotito says he won't be blackmailed into selling the club, nor will he give away tickets for free or at knockdown prices to artificially fill the stands. He merely says: "We're top of the table. If you love Lazio, you should be in the stadium instead of leaving the players to fend for themselves."
The boycott will be suspended for the derby against Roma next month -- staying home for that one would be a step too far -- but beyond that it's going to be business as usual, and the fans seem undeterred. Not to mention that, whatever they're doing seems to be working both in terms of results and reawakening the fanbase.
Will Lazio still be top come the end of the season? Probably not. The schedule has been relatively kind to them thus far, and their underlying metrics suggest regression to the mean. They're greatly outperforming xG, both in goals scored (25 on 17.3 xG) and conceded (nine against an xGC of 13.6), and top-to-bottom, this doesn't seem a particularly talented side. Some have compared them to the Leicester City side that won the Premier League in 2015-16, but while Fratessi, Mattia Zaccagni and Kenneth Taylor are fine players, Belahayne and Provstgaard have been revelations and Mandas is having a monster season, there's no obvious Jamie Vardy , N'Golo Kanté or Riyad Mahrez here.
Will the boycott work and get Lotito to sell the club? This one's more complex and perhaps of interest to fans of Manchester United , Valencia and any club with an unpopular owner.
The reality is that Lotito is a particularly unpleasant and stubborn nut to crack. He's had credible death threats over the years, which is why he travels with armed bodyguards, yet seems entirely unfazed.

headline: Lazio lidera Serie A
caption: A pesar del boicot de sus hinchas, Lazio se encuentra en el primer lugar de la Serie A con 32 puntos en 12 partidos, su mejor inicio en más de 25 años. Los hinchas están boicoteando al equipo debido a su descontento con el dueño del club, Claudio Lotito.

title: Resultados de la quinta fecha de la Champions League y posiciones
description: Se juega una nueva jornada liguera de la Orejona. Acá, los marcadores y cómo está la tabla.
article_context:
Con presencia de varios argentinos, este martes se puso en marcha la quinta fecha de la fase regular de la Champions League. 18 partidos en total. Se sabe, al cabo de ocho fechas, los mejores ocho se meterán en los octavos de final, y, del puesto nueve al 24, jugarán por playoffs para completar los cupos restantes de octavos. A continuación, los marcadores y cómo sigue el miércoles.
Este miércoles, e l Atlético de Madrid llegará obligado ante el Viking: el equipo de los Simeone y la banda argentina, necesita sumar para no quedar más relegado. Además, el Liverpool de Mac Allister visita al Brujas y el Inter (seguramente con Lautaro Martínez de arranque) recibe al Stuttgart.
Los otros dos grandes cruces del miércoles tendrán como protagonistas a la Roma (con Dybala, Nahuel Molina, Balerdi, Soulé y Santi Castro) ante el bicampeón y con puntaje ideal PSG (llega con lesiones graves en la temporada). Además, el Manchester United en crisis, con Pochettino recién llegado y Licha Martínez, va a Portugal para jugar con el Sporting en Lisboa.

title: How B.J. Callaghan's long, winding coaching journey led to Nashville success
description: Callaghan was a fairly unassuming hire when he took over Nashville. Now he's a Supporters' Shield-winning coach being linked with the USMNT job.
article_context:
In the spring of 2003, B.J. Callaghan made one of those fateful decisions that can define a life.
He was just months away from finishing his economics degree at Ursinus College, where he had played goalkeeper on the soccer team. It was time to enter the working world.
Callaghan went on his first interview and had what amounted to an epiphany. A corporate job wasn't for him. He tested the theory a second time with another job interview. The result was the same. But if he didn't enter the corporate world, what would he do?
"I was taking a minor in coaching while I was in college," Callaghan told ESPN, half joking. "So it was more like there were a lot of signals to me saying, 'You should be a coach.' And I think there was still part of my brain saying, 'Man, I should really be in the business world because that's what you're supposed to do.' And I walked away from those two interviews. I had spoken to my current college coach and told him that, and he kind of laughed and said, 'Yeah, we all kind of know that you should probably be [coaching].'"
Callaghan followed that advice, and over the course of 23 years, hit the motherlode. He worked his way through the youth, college, academy, professional and national team ranks, all the way to his current position as head coach of Nashville SC .
He hasn't been just getting by with NSC, either. One year after leading the Coyotes to the U.S. Open Cup title, their first trophy since the organization joined MLS in 2020, he led Nashville to this year's Supporters' Shield, emblematic of the league's highest points total.
Now he not only has an MLS Cup in his sights, but his name is being bandied about as a possible replacement for Mauricio Pochettino with the U.S. men's national team . Suffice it to say, Callaghan made the right decision.
"You reflect back on the journey and you pick up so many different things, you meet so many different people and so many people along the way invest in you and believe in you and push you and continue to motivate you to keep going," Callaghan said. "I think there is an element of anybody in this profession, you have to have this willingness to maybe take risks a little bit, but at the same time you're doing it because you're betting on yourself and you believe in yourself."
Part of what gave Callaghan the impetus to be a coach was that it was in the blood to a degree. Callaghan's grandfather, Jack Kraft, was a legendary college basketball coach at Villanova, reaching the NCAA tournament six times and the NIT another five.
That's not to say Callaghan becoming a coach was preordained. It was more a seed that was planted thanks to being part of a sports family. There would be little in the way of pushback from Callaghan's parents about his budding career choice.
"I think you understood that [coaching] was a real thing to have as a profession," Callaghan said about his family. "I think that was much more the confidence to do it and to pursue it and to understand you have to take it really seriously, and you have to work at it and you have to develop it and there's step by step that you have to do."
Callaghan's time at Ursinus proved formative as well. He arrived on campus in August 1999, and as a goalkeeper, made an immediate impression on his teammates. With a height under 6-foot, Callaghan wasn't the most physically imposing goalkeeper, but he compensated in plenty of other ways.
"I guess you would call it fresh energy," said Kevin Poust, 47, a teammate of Callaghan's at Ursinus and now a data analyst. "[Callaghan] was always hyped. He was always positive and very loud. You heard B.J., you knew when he was in the room, that's for sure. And that was every day."
Mike Papenberg, 45, another college teammate of Callaghan's, who is now the athletic director at Palmyra High School in New Jersey, noted that Callaghan's communication was always constructive, and he was more than willing to put his body on the line.
"He was fearless. He's like a pit bull," Papenberg said about Callaghan. "He's not the biggest guy, but he was not afraid of anybody or anything. If he needed to come out and throw a punch to get a ball out off a corner kick or a set piece, he was coming out and throwing that punch."
Callaghan's lack of fear manifested itself in unique ways. Poust recalled how a house they were renting had a flat roof, so Callaghan and his housemates made a big pile of leaves and proceeded to jump off the roof into the pile, taking the old Tom Petty lyric -- "I'm learning to fly, but I ain't got wings" -- a bit too literally.
"We ended up getting in trouble for that," said Poust. "But I remember B.J. flying off and we had to put a mattress [on the pile] because the leaves started to get matted down. He must have bounced like five feet in the air off the mattress because he did a belly flop. No fear right there."
Callaghan's time as a college goalkeeper helped lay the foundation for his coaching mind. He had the best view of the field and was adept at putting his teammates in the positions they needed to be in. He could see things almost before they happened.
"I think the way I looked at the position was trying to understand that it's more about the group in front of you," he said. "There's a little bit of selflessness that comes in because you're counting on 10 other guys to help you before you have to do your job. But at the same time, I think as a coach, there's a massive level of accountability that you have to take. And as a goalkeeper, it's pretty much like, that's the job: accountability."
Armed with that tactical foundation, as well as his lack of fear, Callaghan dove into the coaching ranks. He started at Ursinus before moving to St. Joseph's University as an assistant with the women's program.
He did the same at Villanova before crossing over to the men's program. It helped that he had his wife, Leigh, by his side. Callaghan admits that those early coaching gigs didn't pay well, and Leigh's job in the pharmaceutical industry, not to mention the emotional encouragement she provided, helped him navigate the ups and downs.
"That support, I think, has always been the loving, encouraging, pushing, motivating, whatever you kind of needed at that time," said Callaghan about Leigh. "So there was emotional support. There was obviously family support and glue. And I think there was also, at points in time, it was definitely financial as well. And I think credit to her, she's done that all while being highly successful in her ow
headline: B.J. Callaghan lleva a Nashville al Supporters' Shield, vinculado al USMNT
caption: B.J. Callaghan, quien llegó a Nashville SC como un fichaje discreto, condujo al equipo a conquistar el Supporters' Shield, el mayor puntaje de la MLS. Tras ese logro, su nombre aparece como posible sustituto del técnico de la selección masculina de EE. UU., el USMNT. El éxito se suma a una trayectoria de 23 años que pasó por categorías juveniles, universitarias, academias y selecciones nacionales, incluida una victoria en la U.S. Open Cup.

title: Højgaard sinks 25-foot putt on final hole for share of RSM Classic lead
description: Rasmus Hojgaard made a 25-foot birdie putt on the last hole for a 5-under 65, giving him a share of the 54-hole lead at the rain-delayed RSM Classic.
article_context:
ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. -- Rasmus Højgaard took an important step toward keeping his PGA Tour card when he made a 25-foot birdie putt on the last hole for a 5-under 65 on Sunday, giving him a share of the 54-hole lead with Michael Thorbjornsen at the rain-delayed RSM Classic.
Thorbjornsen was atop the leaderboard for most of the cool, cloudy day at Sea Island. The American shot a 66 to join the Danish player at 13-under 199.
Thorbjornsen is among those who have little pressure outside of trying to win the final event of the season. He won the Rocket Classic this summer to secure a spot in the Masters and a PGA Tour card through 2028.
Højgaard, who played for Europe's winning Ryder Cup team last year, is at No. 122 in the FedEx Cup. The top 100 are assured of full status.
"Today felt very free. Tomorrow is a completely different day," Højgaard said. "I think, yeah, I'm going to feel the stress, I'm going to feel the nerves. Again, I think that's what we all play for is to put ourselves in those positions, and we'll see what happens."
Max Greyserman was likely safe at No. 91 in the FedEx Cup. He shot a 65 and was one shot off the lead as he goes for his first PGA Tour title.
The group two shots behind -- Max McGreevy (67), Haotong Li (67) and Marco Penge (68) -- all are outside the top 100 with a lot on the line Monday.
The tournament was washed out by heavy rain on Saturday, leading to the final round being held on Monday at Sea Island. It will be the second straight Monday finish on the PGA Tour. The Austin Championship last week also was delayed by rain.
Jackson Koivun , who won this summer in Minnesota right out of college, shot 65 and was three shots behind. Already in the Masters and PGA Championship, Koivun would earn an exemption into the U.S. Open with a victory at the RSM Classic.
Brooks Koepka had some adventures on the fourth hole when he made triple bogey but recovered to finish five shots behind after a 67. Koepka is a five-time major champion. Far more pressure falls to two others at 8-under 204 -- David Ford and Davis Thompson , who lives at Sea Island and whose father is the tournament director.
headline: Højgaard empata liderato del RSM Classic con birdie de 25 pies
caption: Rasmus Højgaard realizó un putt de birdie de 25 pies en el último hoyo, logrando 5 bajo 65 y compartiendo la ventaja de 54 hoyos con Michael Thorbjornsen en el RSM Classic, retrasado por lluvia en Sea Island. Ambos están a 13 bajo 199. Thorbjornsen, ganador del Rocket Classic, ya aseguró su tarjeta del PGA Tour hasta 2028, mientras Højgaard, que jugó en la Ryder Cup, busca mantener su tarjeta, pues está 122 en la clasificación FedEx Cup, donde los 100 primeros garantizan estatus completo.

title: Alivio para el United: la FA le anuló la roja a Leny Yoro y podrá jugar el próximo partido
description: El defensor francés fue expulsado ante Liverpool por una falta sobre Alexander Isak, pero los Diablos Rojos consiguieron que se revirtiera la sanción.
article_context:
Roja a Yoro ante el Liverpool. (Getty Images)
L a derrota por 4-0 frente a Liverpool , con el debut de Mauricio Pochettino, dejó varias cuestiones para el Manchester United , pero una de ellas ya se resolvió. La Federación Inglesa de Fútbol aceptó el reclamo del club y anuló la tarjeta roja que había recibido Leny Yoro durante ese encuentro . De esta manera, el defensor francés estará disponible para el próximo partido.
La expulsión fue a los ocho minutos del encuentro , cuando el árbitro Sam Barrott consideró que Yoro había empujado desde atrás a Alexander Isak , quien estaba de cara al arco y tenía una clara oportunidad de gol . Al entender que el francés era el último hombre, el juez le mostró la roja directa.
Sin embargo, desde el United no estuvieron de acuerdo con la decisión y apelaron ante las autoridades. El argumento principal de los de Manchester fue que, si bien hubo un contacto entre los futbolistas, Isak ya no estaba en control del balón y el arquero Senne Lammens tenía la pelota bajo su dominio.
La federación inglesa confirmó que aceptó la apelación presentada por el club rojo de Manchester y que el defensor no tendrá que cumplir con la fecha de suspensión que correspondía a la expulsión.
" La suspensión de un partido de Leny Yoro fue levantada tras una apelación exitosa por expulsión injustificada . El jugador del Manchester United fue expulsado por impedir una clara ocasión de gol durante el partido de la Premier League contra el Liverpool el domingo 22 de noviembre. La Comisión Reguladora Independiente publicará próximamente los motivos por escrito de la decisión", informó el club.
Con esta resolución, el francés quedó habilitado para volver a jugar y podrá ser parte del equipo que enfrente al Brentford este sábado 28 en Old Trafford , desde las 12.00 (hora argentina).
Leny Yoro fue expulsado por esta infracción vs. Liverpool (Video: ESPN).
Yoro no fue el único caso de este tipo en el fútbol inglés durante las últimas semanas . El 14 de octubre, la FA también anuló la sanción por la expulsión de Pascal Struijk , defensor del Brighton , por una infracción sobre Wilson Isidor en el encuentro frente al Sunderland, disputado cuatro días antes.
En aquella oportunidad, el árbitro Thomas Bramall fue convocado por el VAR, a cargo de Neil Davies, para revisar la jugada. Después de ver varias veces las imágenes, el juez decidió mostrarle la tarjeta roja al neerlandés, considerando que había impedido una ocasión clara de gol . El club presentó una apelación por expulsión injustificada y consiguió que se le quitara la sanción.

headline: FA anula roja a Leny Yoro y podrá jugar
caption: La Federación Inglesa de Fútbol aceptó la apelación del Manchester United y anuló la tarjeta roja que le había impuesto al defensor francés Leny Yoro en el partido contra Liverpool. Con la sanción revocada, Yoro podrá alistarse para el próximo encuentro del United ante Brentford, programado para el sábado 28 en Old Trafford.

headline: Deniz Gul anota tarde y condena a Aston Villa

title: Colapinto avisó que Qatar va a ser diferente a Las Vegas: "Volveremos a ver una carrera más normal"
description: El piloto de Alpine comenzó a palpitar la próxima fecha de la Fórmula 1 y anticipó que no se van a ver los trencitos eternos que se produjeron en el callejero estadounidense.
article_context:
Franco Colapinto sigue contento. Risueño. Se sube al avión con el casco en la mano, apoya la cabeza en el asiento y recuerda los adelantamientos a los McLaren, las batallas con los pilotos de punta y el sexto puesto en el GP de Las Vegas , que seguramente ya atesoró en un lugar especial de su corazón. Pero en la Fórmula 1 hay que seguir, y hay semanas como estas en las que los corredores no tienen respiro: de inmediato, los 22 autos de la Máxima se dirigirán a Lusail, donde se disputará el GP de Qatar , que el bonaerense imagina que no se parecerá en nada al show estadounidense...
"Fue fantástico volver a sumar puntos en Las Vegas e igualar mi mejor resultado hasta la fecha en la Fórmula 1. Tuvimos un buen ritmo durante todo el fin de semana, ya que diversas características del circuito se adaptaron bien a nuestro monoplaza, y gestionamos el evento a la perfección con ambos coches. Esperamos mantener el impulso en Qatar ", pidió el corredor de 22 años.
Palpitando lo que pasará en el Circuito Internacional de Lusail, y cómo espera que se dé, siguió: "Probablemente volveremos a un tipo de carrera más normal , tras la intensa dinámica de succión que acabamos de vivir, que resultó ser algo muy singular".
¿Cuál será la clave? En pocas palabras, por cómo es este trazado, no equivocarse. "El trazado castiga mucho los errores , con las escapatorias de grava situadas muy cerca de la salida de las curvas; cada vez que te abrís lo pagás. Pero el flujo de las curvas hace que completar una vuelta sea una experiencia muy gratificante. Estamos preparados para darlo todo de nuevo en la penúltima cita del año y, ojalá, lograr puntuar por segunda carrera consecutiva".
Caroline Smith coincidió con Franco en el vuelo de vuelta de Las Vegas y compartió el video en redes sociales. Video: @itscarolinescorner

headline: Colapinto anticipa una carrera más normal en Qatar tras Las Vegas
caption: El argentino de Alpine igualó en Las Vegas su mejor resultado en la Fórmula 1 con un sexto puesto y quiere repetir el puntaje en Lusail, la penúltima fecha del año. Avisa que Qatar no tendrá los trencitos eternos de autos pegados que vio el callejero estadounidense, y que el trazado castiga cada error con la grava muy cerca de la salida de las curvas. ¿Podrá sostener el envión en un circuito que no perdona nada?

title: La Selección Argentina de talla baja aplastó a Brasil en el Mundial de Marruecos y espera rival en cuartos
description: Con póker de Lucas Deamigo, el vigente campeón goleó 5-1 a la Canarinha, cerró su zona como líder invicto y ya palpita el mata-mata del torneo en África.
article_context:
La selección Argentina de talla baja, es la campeona defensora del Mundial.
La Selección Argentina de talla baja sigue a paso firme en la defensa de su título mundial. Tras consagrarse en la primera edición del certamen en 2023, la Albiceleste busca el bicampeonato en Marruecos y, este martes 24, goleó por 5-1 a Brasil en el cierre de la fase de grupos. Con cuatro tantos de Lucas Deamigo y uno de Martín Antúnez, el conjunto nacional consiguió su tercera victoria consecutiva y se aseguró el primer puesto de su zona .
Pese a comenzar en desventaja ante la Canarinha, la Albiceleste logró revertir el resultado y terminó imponiéndose con contundencia ante su clásico rival. De esta manera, Argentina cerró la primera instancia del certamen con tres victorias en igual cantidad de presentaciones.
Con este triunfo por 5-1 frente a Brasil , el campeón defensor venció a todos sus rivales adentro de la cancha, y acabó con 13 goles a favor y apenas dos en contra. De esta manera, logró avanzar a los cuartos de final como líder de su grupo .
El seleccionado argentino había iniciado su participación en el Mundial con una goleada por 5-0 ante Jordania, mientras que en su segunda presentación venció por 3-1 a Irak, y se aseguró el primer lugar .
Con el primer puesto de su zona asegurado, la Selección Argentina volverá a jugar este jueves 26 de noviembre , desde las 16.15 (hora argentina), cuando se mida ante el segundo del Grupo 4, integrado por Paraguay, Egipto, Japón y Ghana. En caso de avanzar, disputará las semifinales el viernes 27, mientras que la final está programada para el domingo 29.
Por el momento, Paraguay y Egipto lideran el Grupo 4 con seis puntos cada uno. Ambas selecciones se enfrentarán en la última jornada de la fase de grupos, en un duelo que definirá las posiciones de la zona y, por lo tanto, al próximo rival de Argentina , que se medirá ante el equipo que finalice segundo.
La participación de la Selección Argentina de talla baja en el Mundial de Marruecos estuvo marcada por las dificultades económicas que atravesó el plantel para afrontar los gastos del viaje . Tras varias semanas de colectas y campañas en redes sociales, al combinado nacional todavía le faltaba cubrir uno de los pasajes de la delegación.
Fue entonces cuando apareció Marcos Senesi . El defensor del Tottenham, que formó parte del plantel de Lionel Scaloni que disputó el último Mundial, realizó junto a su familia una donación que permitió completar los fondos necesarios para que todos los integrantes del seleccionado pudieran viajar a Marruecos.
Antes de partir desde el aeropuerto de Ezeiza, los futbolistas publicaron un video en sus redes sociales en el que agradecieron a quienes colaboraron con la causa , con una mención especial para el ex San Lorenzo. “ Se puso la 10, se puso la camiseta de la igualdad y de la integración ”, expresó Facundo Rojas, capitán del conjunto nacional.

headline: Argentina de talla baja derrota a Brasil y avanza a cuartos
caption: Con cuatro goles de Lucas Deamigo y uno de Martín Antúnez, la selección Argentina de talla baja superó 5-1 a Brasil, cerró la fase de grupos como líder invicto y aseguró su puesto en los cuartos de final del Mundial de Marruecos. title: Lehecka, Czechs beat Canada, reach Davis Cup semifinals
description: Jiri Lehecka led the Czech Republic into the Davis Cup semifinals, beating Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6 (4), 6-2 on Tuesday to complete a 2-0 victory over Canada.
article_context:
Jiri Lehecka led the Czech Republic into the Davis Cup semifinals, beating Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6 (4), 6-2 on Tuesday to complete a 2-0 victory over Canada.
The 14th-ranked Lehecka saved all nine break points he faced in the first set, and never allowed another as he took two of the eight break chances he created in the second set.
Earlier, the Czechs took the opening match when 60th-ranked Tomas Machac beat No. 165 Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2.
The fourth-seeded Czechs next face top-seeded Italy or South Korea, who meet in their quarterfinal Wednesday.
The other quarterfinals matchups Thursday are Spain with Carlos Alcaraz vs. Austria and top-ranked Alexander Zverev's Germany vs. Britain.
headline: Lehecka lleva a República Checa a semifinales de la Davis Cup
caption: Jiri Lehecka impulsó a la República Checa a la semifinal del Davis Cup al vencer a Felix Auger‑Aliassime 7‑6 (4), 6‑2, completando una victoria 2‑0 sobre Canadá. El checo, con el puesto 14, salvó los nueve puntos de quiebre del primer set y rompió dos de sus ocho oportunidades en el segundo. Anteriormente, Tomas Machac había ganado su partido contra Liam Draxl, asegurando el dominio checo. Los cuartos de final los decidirán Italia o Corea del Sur, mientras que España y Alemania se enfrentarán a sus rivales respectivos.

title: Operación exitosa para Aníbal Moreno de su lesión en la zona lumbar: cómo será su rehabilitación y cuándo podría volver a jugar en River
description: El volante central pasó por el quirófano este martes a la tarde y comenzará la recuperación con el objetivo de iniciar la pretemporada a la par del plantel.
article_context:
Aníbal Moreno, volante central de River (Instagram).
Primer paso cumplido para dejar atrás un calvario físico que lo tuvo a maltraer durante casi todo el segundo semestre de 2026. Este martes a la tarde, Aníbal Moreno fue intervenido quirúrgicamente con éxito de la protrusión discal en la zona lumbar que le permitió jugar apenas 705 minutos en nueve partidos después del receso por el Mundial. De esta manera, el volante central de River , de 27 años, comenzará con su rehabilitación desde este miércoles con el objetivo de iniciar la pretemporada de enero a la par del plantel que hoy dirige Leonardo Ponzio , quien solamente pudo utilzar al ex Palmeiras los 90' del 3-0 contra Belgrano y 17' en el clásico frente a Racing.
El problema en la parte baja de la espalda —una discopatía localizada entre la última vértebra lumbar y el sacro — comenzó a fines de agosto, inmediatamente después de la eliminación de River de la Copa Sudamericana frente a Independiente Santa Fe. Aquel episodio dejó al mediocampista catamarqueño 53 días sin actividad oficial y afuera de seis partidos consecutivos del Torneo Clausura (Banfield, Independiente Rivadavia, Atlético Tucumán, Huracán, Estudiantes de La Plata y Sarmiento), período en el que realizó un tratamiento conservador con kinesiología y ejercicios posturales en el gimnasio.
Recuperado momentáneamente de los dolores más agudos, Moreno reapareció como titular el 18 de octubre en la goleada 3-0 frente a Belgrano en Córdoba, donde logró completar el partido. Sin embargo, una semana más tarde —el 25 de octubre, en el clásico contra su exequipo, Racing, en el Monumental— sufrió una fuerte recaída y debió pedir el cambio entre lágrimas a los 17' minutos del primer tiempo.
A partir de ese momento no pudo volver a jugar Aníbal Moreno : se perdió el superclásico en la Bombonera , la visita ante Aldosivi y el mata-mata de octavos contra Lanús. Si bien en las semanas posteriores a resentirse de la lasión intentó evitar el quirófano apelando a sesiones de fisioterapia e infiltraciones mediante "bloqueos" lumbares para calmar el dolor, los procedimientos alternativos no lograron resolver la afección de raíz. Entonces, ante la persistencia de las molestias y el riesgo que implica una lesión crónica en una zona tan delicada como la columna, entre el cuerpo médico de River y el propio futbolista consensuaron recurrir a la cirugía para solucionar definitivamente la patología y encarar un 2027 desde cero.
En principio, Moreno tendrá que hacer un reposo de alrededor de un mes mientras realice sesiones de kinesiología y determinados ejercicios con escasa movilidad que le permitan ir recuperando la masa muscular que naturalmente perderá durante el proceso inicial de la recuperación. El paso siguiente será un intenso trabajo en el gimnasio y en la movilidad de todo su cuerpo, para luego empezar lentamente con ejercicios en el campo que debería aumentar durante el periodo de vacaciones del equipo para sumar chances de arrancar la pretemporada de verano al mismo ritmo que sus compañeros.

headline: Aníbal Moreno operado de lumbar, busca iniciar pretemporada
caption: Aníbal Moreno, volante central de River, se sometió a una cirugía exitosa por una protrusión discal en la zona lumbar. A partir de mañana iniciará su rehabilitación con sesiones de kinesiología y ejercicios de baja movilidad, con el objetivo de reincorporarse al plantel y comenzar la pretemporada de enero junto a sus compañeros bajo la dirección de Leonardo Ponzio. La intervención busca evitar una lesión crónica y permitirle retomar la actividad competitiva en 2027.

title: Dybala en un deseo que ¿le cierra la puerta a Boca?
description: Paulo contó que tiene la intención de terminar su carrera en el fútbol italiano. "Espero que sí, para mí sería muy lindo", afirmó. Aunque también aclaró: "Después veremos".
article_context:
Paulo Dybala pasó por la conferencia de prensa previa al partido que la Roma jugará este miércoles, a las 17.00, ante el PSG en París por la Champions League . Y formuló una declaración que parece que cierra la expectativa de un regreso al fútbol argentino. Un periodista le consultó por una frase en la web de la UEFA sobre su deseo de finalizar su carrera en el Calcio y la respuesta resultó contundente.
"Espero que sí, para mí sería muy lindo, como dije ahí. Llegué con 18 años y no me veo en otro lado, pero el fútbol cambia mucho, a veces cambia de golpe, sobre todo en este fútbol más moderno, digamos, donde hay muchos movimientos. Pero disfruto ahora, me queda un año de contrato acá y disfruto este momento, de lo que está haciendo el equipo y después veremos", fue su respuesta.
A su lado estaba el técnico del Giallorosso, Gian Piero Gasperini, que le consultó si podría ser en otro equipo de Italia, y se permitió sonreír.
El futbolista de la Roma habló en la previa de enfrentar al PSG por la Champions League.
Recordar: varias veces se instaló la posibilidad de que se sume a Boca, club del que confesó ser hincha y en el cual juega Leandro Paredes, excompañero en la Selección Argentina y también en la Roma, un vínculo que potenciaba una incorporación. Esta frase relativiza esa chance, aunque tampoco resulta taxativa porque aclara: "Después veremos".
Paulo se incorporó de Instituto a Palermo en 2012. En 2015 pasó a la Juventus, donde jugó siete temporadas. Desde 2022 es parte del equipo capitalino. Tiene 33 años.
Sobre su estado físico, declaró: "En este momento me siento bien. No tuve tantos problemas durante el período de la lesión, también porque después hubo la pausa y pude trabajar dos semanas con el equipo. Me sentí bien en los minutos que jugué contra el Parma y, seguramente, con el tiempo, partido tras partido, me sentiré cada vez mejor".
Le preguntaron si en el plantel de la Roma hay ambiente ganador. "En los años en los que estuve en Italia, sobre todo en la Juventus, tuve la posibilidad de ganar. Lo entendés más adelante, porque todavía es pronto para decir si somos un equipo que puede ganar. Creo que hay equipos fuertes en la Serie A que tienen seguramente más experiencia en ganar. Pero somos conscientes de ser un equipo fuerte, con valores. Tenemos un grupo muy sano, muy bonito, y esto muchas veces ayuda a ganar. Este año lo estamos haciendo bien. Ahora llegan muchos partidos difíciles, pero debemos continuar haciendo lo que estamos haciendo. Es lo que te puedo decir. Después, seguramente más adelante veremos si estamos en el camino correcto para aspirar a algo más".
Lo consultaron por qué patea menos al arco. "Yo siempre digo que ahora pateo menos porque al míster le gusta que metamos el pase cuando estamos cerca del área, y además (Donyell) Malen está bien. Pienso que es una cuestión de partidos, no creo haber pateado menos. Creo que a veces busqué la mejor solución, la de encontrar a un compañero dentro del área. He rematado en algunos partidos, pero todavía no he encontrado el gol, así que tal vez por eso piensan que tiro menos. Yo estoy tranquilo, sé que tuve esta lesión, que llegó en un momento en el que ni siquiera me lo esperaba, porque me sentía en uno de los mejores momentos del último año".

title: Las 1000 Millas Sport vuelven a la Patagonia con nuevas pruebas y autos de lujo: Bugatti, Aston Martin, Ferrari y más
description: Del 25 al 29 de noviembre, en Bariloche, se pondrá en marcha la 37ª edición de una de las competencias sport más emblemáticas de Latinoamérica.
article_context:
El recorrido pasará por el emblemático Hotel Llao Llao de Bariloche (prensa 1000 Millas Sport).
Las 1000 Millas Sport , la competencia de regularidad más emblemática de Latinoamérica, organizada por el Club de Automóviles Sport (CAS), se prepara para una nueva edición que se llevará adelante del 25 al 29 de noviembre en la Patagonia ; con un recorrido que volverá a combinar regularidad, paisajes únicos y una grilla internacional de autos sport clásicos.
Una de las principales novedades de esta 37ª edición será la incorporación de nuevas pruebas de regularidad, que elevarán el desafío para las distintas tripulaciones. “Nos gusta reinterpretar la propuesta en cada edición. Siempre hay caminos por descubrir y paisajes nuevos por recorrer. Este año en particular, incorporamos pruebas de regularidad que van a poner a prueba hasta a los competidores más experimentados ”, explicó Fernando Briones, presidente del CAS y del Comité Organizador.
Las 1000 Millas Sport son más que una competencia. Año a año, pilotos y copilotos de distintas partes del mundo se dan cita para revivir el espíritu de las competencias sport clásicas y rendir tributo a los verdaderos protagonistas: los vehículos sport clásicos que reviven la historia en cada ruta de la patagonia. La competencia, que inicia y culmina en el emblemático Hotel Llao Llao de Bariloche y pasa por lugares como Dina Huapi, Villa La Angostura, Reserva Natural, 7 Lagos, Villa Mascardi y El Bolsón, entre otros, y combina espíritu deportivo, historia, gastronomía y paisajes únicos.
Los participantes recorren miles de kilómetros disfrutando del manejo y la camaradería, mientras ponen a prueba lo más relevante de la competencia: la regularidad , que es el corazón de las 1000 Millas Sport. Así lo explicó Daniel Claramunt, director ejecutivo de las 1000 Millas Sport: “La regularidad exige una conexión total entre el piloto y su navegante” .
La edición 2026 ya cuenta con tripulaciones confirmadas de Estados Unidos, Alemania, Suiza, Chile y Uruguay, además de participantes argentinos. “La grilla va a ser un espectáculo visual”, adelanta Briones. Contará con la presencia de verdaderos íconos: Mercedes Benz 300SL, Aston Martin DB5, Bugatti T37, Ferrari 365GTC. BMW 328, entre otras grandes joyas del automovilismo histórico.
El recorrido volverá a atravesar algunos de los paisajes y localidades más representativos de la región, con nuevos puntos de parada para almuerzos y refrigerios. “El entorno patagónico es la escenografía perfecta y acompaña en toda la competencia” , sostiene Briones.
Para el público, el tradicional Parque Cerrado del Centro Cívico de Bariloche será nuevamente uno de los grandes puntos de encuentro , mientras que el paso por San Martín de los Andes y Villa La Angostura ofrecerá diferentes lugares panorámicos para ver los vehículos en competencia.
Las 1000 Millas Sport también mantienen su compromiso con las comunidades que reciben a la competencia. El tradicional remate solidario beneficia al Banco de Alimentos y a distintas organizaciones locales , mientras que en los últimos seis años la organización profundizó su vínculo con entidades de la región como Fundación Challenge, Puentes de Luz y Fundación Cruzada Patagónica. El objetivo es que el paso de la competencia por la Patagonia trascienda el espectáculo automovilístico y genere un impacto concreto y sostenible en las comunidades locales .

headline: Las 1000 Millas Sport vuelven a Bariloche con nuevas pruebas

La organización sumó nuevas pruebas de regularidad que, según Fernando Briones, presidente del Club de Automóviles Sport, pondrán a prueba incluso a los más experimentados. title: Oxford beat Spurs U21s to seal EFL Trophy progress
description: Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Under-21s to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.
article_context:
Aaron Ramsey is experiencing the EFL Trophy for the first time in his football career
Aaron Ramsey's Oxford United beat Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1 to secure one of the final two Jersey Mike's Trophy knockout spots.
Oxford knew avoiding defeat by a margin of four goals or more would be enough to seal progression from Southern Group A alongside already-qualified Exeter City.
They trailed to Tyler Tingey's early opener on Tuesday, which gave Spurs' youngsters a glimmer of hope of pulling off that mini-miracle.
But Jun'ai Byfield's own goal and 18-year-old Jack Lee's late winner ensured ex-Arsenal man Ramsey got one over his old north London rivals as Oxford won to finish top of the group.
Elsewhere, Fleetwood's decisive Northern Group G match at home to Leeds United Under-21s was put back 24 hours because of a waterlogged pitch.
The two sides will now meet on Wednesday to decide who progresses alongside group leaders Oldham Athletic to complete the line-up for the knockout stages.
There were wins for League Two pair Tranmere Rovers and Salford City over Premier League sides in Tuesday's other two ties, which were virtually dead rubbers.
Tranmere, who had already sealed their last-32 spot, came from behind to beat eliminated Everton Under-21s 2-1 with goals from David Kamara and Charlie Veevers in Northern Group E.
Both Salford City and Sunderland Under-21s had already been eliminated from Northern Group A but goals from Paolo Mariani, Brandon Cooper and Kyrell Malcolm gave the Ammies a 3-2 win despite Jaydon Jones' Black Cats double.
Of the 16 Premier League under-21 sides to enter the competition, with one placed in each group, only six have progressed to the knockout rounds, although Leeds can still make that number seven.
The last-32 draw will take place on Wednesday at 16:30 GMT. Ties will take place in the week commencing 7 December.
All 16 group winners are guaranteed a home tie, with fixtures remaining regionalised until the semi-final stage.

title: La nueva estrategia de mercado de River: el plan para captar jóvenes talentos antes que Europa
description: Además de los refuerzos puntuales que se buscarán, la dirigencia también apuntará a futuro en el verano. El rol de Longoria y el apellido que ya gusta.
article_context:
Longoria y su equipo son los encargados del scout.
Parece lejano hablar del mercado de pases cuando el fin de semana se disputan los cuartos de final del Clausura, con todo lo que eso implica para River . No es tan necesario aclarar todo lo que puede pasar en caso de una eliminación o evitarse si se sigue en competencia. Pero la dirigencia también entiende que, luego de un año complejo en cuanto a resultados, mirar hacia el futuro y empezar a diseñarlo es clave. Por eso, en este verano se verá una nueva estrategia para contrataciones de jugadores ...
Esto será independiente de las posiciones en las que se buscará incorporar para reforzar el equipo: al menos un zaguero y un volante central , probablemente la zona ofensiva y un arquero en caso de que se vaya Santiago Beltrán. Así, la idea es que mientras se gestionan apellidos para esos lugares, se pueda apostar por algunos jugadores más prometedores que hoy son muy jóvenes y no tan conocidos para el mundo del fútbol en general.
La nueva metodología, encabezada por el director deportivo Pablo Longoria y su equipo de scouting desde hace un tiempo y en secreto, consta en detectar a talentos incipientes que todavía no sobresalieron en sus ligas para adelantarse a los europeos que vienen a comprar al continente. En otras palabras, pasar a ser ese "europeo" para darles la última etapa de formación a los jóvenes (mayoritaria y preferentemente menores a 19 años) con la metodología River y poder disfrutarlos en el futuro.
Si bien la cantidad de incorporaciones de este estilo dependerá de las oportunidades que se vayan dando en el mercado y de cómo se utilice el presupuesto previsto para el fútbol profesional (saldrá de los aproximadamente u$s 12 millones que se destinarán, que se pueden ampliar en caso de una venta), no todos los que lleguen se quedarán en el plantel principal : está previsto que alguno de menor edad pueda sumar rodaje en la Reserva y que otros sean cedidos para que vayan incorporando experiencia y minutos en equipos de Primera o mismo del exterior. El plan es, luego, poder tenerlos en el equipo y asegurar un recambio juvenil, o bien directamente sacarles un rédito económico .
Naturalmente, estos nombres que están en la carpeta de Longoria y el también español Domingo Catoira (se sumó a mediados de año para abarcar mejor el área de scouting) no requerirán de grandes erogaciones económicas : por más que desde las oficinas del Monumental aún no se animan a ponerle tope a un jugador (cada caso es diferente, lógicamente), aseguran que serán inversiones bajas y, dependiendo cómo se presenten las negociaciones, por algún porcentaje mayoritario de la ficha.
En ese sentido, uno de los que se encuentra en la carpeta de seguimiento y que cumple con todos los requisitos previos como para avanzar cuando se abra el mercado veraniego -tal como aseguran en Núñez- es el paraguayo Mauro Coronel . Tiene 18 años, juega de marcador central, es diestro, mide 1,87 metro y milita en Nacional de Paraguay, que tiene intenciones de hacer caja con el que consideran el mejor proyecto defensivo del país . También merodeado por equipos europeos (Brighton y Aston Villa), disputó los recientes Juegos Suramericanos (le ganaron la final a Argentina y él metió el penal definitivo) y en la fecha FIFA pasada fue convocado por primera vez por Gustavo Alfaro y debutó en la goleada 4-1 a Singapur (fue titular), ratificando la gran proyección que le ven.
El propio presidente del club guaraní pasó este interés a lo público: "Es cierto, se han interesado. Hablé con el presidente de la institución la semana pasada y quedamos en una reunión para estos días. El interés es real, aunque todavía no hay una oferta oficial . También hay interés de otra parte del mundo y nosotros vamos a juzgar qué es lo mejor para Mauro y para la institución", contó este martes Enrique Sánchez, en un diálogo con Rock&Pop Paraguay.
De perfil bajo y apegado a la familia, se inició en Inferiores como volante central, pero lo hicieron retroceder en el campo y se consolidó como un zaguero al que le auguran un gran futuro . Y, por si fuera poco, es titular en su equipo (26 partidos en el año, sin goles y con siete amarillas) y fue importante para que Nacional se asegurara el segundo puesto en la anual, que le dio el pase a la fase de grupos de la próxima Libertadores .
Coronel es uno, pero en la lista hay más. Hablar del mercado en este momento puede parecer lejano, pero en River ya trabajan en él y piensan a futuro . Habrá que ver cómo le va con esta nueva estrategia vinculada a los jóvenes...
